articles.title: Many 'sleep foods' are overhyped. Here's what experts say to eat at night instead
articles.summary: Experts share which foods may help you get better sleep, plus when to stop eating if you have reflux or take a GLP-1 medication.
articles.body:
Our experts independently review everything we recommend. If you buy through our links, we may earn commission.

If you find yourself tossing and turning or struggling to fall asleep because of pesky reflux, what you eat in the evening may be playing a role. "Science shows food has a moderate impact on sleep," says Carleara Weiss , a registered nurse, clinician scientist in behavioral sleep medicine and sleep science adviser at Aeroflow Sleep. While no one food will magically correct your sleep troubles, some provide amino acids like tryptophan or minerals like magnesium and potassium that may help produce melatonin or support relaxation.

But before you start planning turkey dinners every night, gastroenterologist Dr. Sameer Berry cautions: "Most of these foods are overhyped. When I rank the popular claims by the quality of evidence behind them, the order runs close to the opposite of their popularity."

So what actually does help? As a registered dietitian, I had some ideas, but since I don't specialize in sleep, I went to the experts. After talking with Berry, Weiss and fellow dietitian Avery Zenker , it became clear that, as with most things, your overall diet and eating habits matter most, though a few foods may help move the needle. Here's how to eat for better sleep, starting with dinner.

Berry says he'd focus on dinner first, and the timing is just as important as the ingredients. Here's what to prioritize:

Build your plate around fiber. " Fiber intake can lead to deeper sleep and fewer sleep interruptions," Berry says. He recommends vegetables, legumes, whole grains and fruit. An easy way to get more is swapping white-flour products for whole-grain or legume-based versions, like chickpea pasta .

Add healthy carbs and lean protein. Berry says both are important parts of a sleep-friendly dinner.

Go easy on saturated fat and added sugar. "These ingredients can worsen sleep quality ," Berry says.

Consider potatoes (including sweet potatoes). They're rich in potassium, a mineral that may help with muscle relaxation and support healthy blood pressure levels .

Try salmon. It contains tryptophan and vitamin B6 , nutrients the brain uses to help build melatonin, and it's one of the best sources of omega-3s DHA and EPA , which play a role in serotonin production.

Keep meal timing consistent. Already eating a balanced dinner? Weiss recommends taking a look at your whole day. "Keeping meal timing consistent from breakfast to dinner can anchor our circadian rhythms and support metabolism and sleep," she explains.

A note on tryptophan: Foods like turkey are known for their tryptophan content, but Berry cautions against overstating their effectiveness. "Turkey has the least support of any claim I hear. It contains about the same tryptophan as chicken, and tryptophan from a protein meal competes with other amino acids for transport into the brain, so very little arrives," he says. This doesn't mean there's no benefit to eating these foods; just temper your expectations.

Safe Catch Wild Pacific Pink Canned Salmon

If you need a snack between dinner and bedtime, Berry recommends keeping it small and simple. As a dietitian, I'd add that the focus should be on fiber and protein, which help keep your blood sugar steady and your stomach from rumbling all night. "Oatmeal with milk, yogurt with fruit or whole-grain toast with nut butter all fit," Berry says.

Timing also matters. "Two to three hours for most people. Eating within this window significantly increases nighttime waking and increases the time it takes to fall asleep," Berry says.

Again, there's no magical food, but some may be better options than others. Here are the ones that came up most often in our expert interviews and in the current research:

Kiwifruit: In small studies, eating two kiwis an hour before bed for four weeks was linked to better sleep, including in a 2023 study of elite athletes. Researchers think kiwi's melatonin, serotonin, antioxidants and folate may play a role, though research is limited and mixed. Berry recommends this small fruit for a different reason: "Two green kiwis a day may improve constipation and abdominal comfort."

Bananas: Weiss includes bananas among her recommendations. They provide potassium and also contain tryptophan and magnesium.

Milk: Ever heard of drinking warm milk before bed? The warmth is mostly comforting, but milk also contains protein, which may help keep blood sugar steady overnight, and tryptophan. More high-quality studies are needed, but a 2025 review of randomized controlled trials found that milk and dairy consumption may improve self-reported sleep quality.

Tart cherries: Tart cherries have long been popular with athletes for exercise recovery and are now gaining attention for their potential to support sleep. Zenker points to a 2025 review suggesting that tart cherry juice may reduce insomnia severity and nighttime waking while increasing total sleep time and sleep efficiency. Berry also sees promise, calling it "a reasonable experiment for someone without reflux or IBS," but cautions that the studies are small and several are industry-funded. He adds that half a cup of juice is a meaningful dose of sugar.

Nuts and seeds: Zenker lists pumpkin seeds among tryptophan-rich foods, and they're also a source of magnesium. Almonds and pistachios are worth considering for their magnesium, healthy fats and fiber. More research is needed, but a 2026 randomized controlled trial found that adults with poor sleep who ate about 2 ounces of raw almonds daily for five months reported better sleep quality than those who ate a calorie-matched snack. However, the study was funded by the Almond Board of California, so take the results with a grain of salt.

Dietitian tip: Buy almonds, pumpkin seeds and unsweetened dried tart cherries in bulk to make your own bedtime trail mix. For more volume, add some plain popcorn. Keep portions to about a small handful.

365 by Whole Foods Market Organic Pumpkin Seeds

Magnesium is an essential mineral that's gaining momentum as a sleep aid because of its role in helping to quiet the mind and relax the body before bedtime. More research is needed, but a small pilot trial found that magnesium supplements improved sleep quality. Magnesium glycinate in particular may help with sleep, partly because of glycine, an amino acid with its own calming properties. Though again, research confirming its effectiveness and dose is thin.

Magnesium supplements are generally safe at recommended doses, but talk with your doctor or a registered dietitian before adding a new supplement to your routine.

What you eat and when you eat before bed matter even more if you have reflux or slow stomach emptying.

"Anyone with slow stomach emptying needs a longer window. That includes gastroparesis, often from diabetes, and people on GLP-1 medications , which delay gastric emptying," Berry says. "For them, a meal that would normally clear in two to three hours may still be sitting in the stomach at bedtime, and reflux and nausea follow."

For reflux, Berry says the evidence is clear that you should wait two to three hours after eating before lying down, and he tells his reflux patients to wait three hours. He points to a randomized trial of 30 reflux patients in which a dinner two hours before bed caused more acid exposure while lying down than the same dinner six hours before bed.

If a late meal is unavoidable, Berry says to keep it small and low in fat, because fat slows stomach emptying.

Elevating the head of your bed may also help, as may other strategies such as alginate-based products , though talk with your gastroenterologist before trying them.

Need some help getting quality shut-eye? Make sure your bedroom is set up for success. At Yahoo, we've tested more than 100 sleep products, from blackout curtains and cooling sheets to mattresses for side sleepers and people with back pain .

Carleara Weiss , PhD, MSH, RN, sleep science adviser at Aeroflow Sleep

Sameer Berry , MD, gastroenterologist, chief medical officer at Oshi Health

articles.title: Pacientes com câncer relatam tratamento interrompido no Andaraí | G1
articles.standfirst: Pacientes estão há meses sem consultas e quimioterapia após sucessivos cancelamentos. Prefeitura afirma que contratou especialistas, mas reconhece dificuldade para preencher todas as vagas.
articles.summary: Pacientes estão há meses sem consultas e quimioterapia após sucessivos cancelamentos. Prefeitura afirma que contratou especialistas, mas reconhece dificuldade para preencher vagas.
articles.body:
Pacientes em tratamento contra o câncer relatam estar sem acompanhamento médico há meses no Hospital Federal do Andaraí, na Zona Norte do Rio de Janeiro. Segundo os relatos, a saída de oncologistas provocou uma sequência de cancelamentos de consultas e deixou pacientes sem previsão de atendimento e, em alguns casos, sem continuidade da quimioterapia.

É o caso de José Luiz Garcia de Andrade, que chegou a ser atendido duas vezes pelo mesmo oncologista. Depois, foi informado de que o médico não trabalhava mais na unidade. Uma nova consulta foi marcada, mas acabou cancelada novamente após a saída de outra profissional.

Em setembro, José Luiz recebeu uma mensagem informando que a consulta prevista para 9 de outubro de 2026 seria desmarcada. O hospital ofereceu um novo atendimento para 21 de setembro, com outra médica. Três dias antes da data remarcada, no entanto, ele recebeu outro aviso: a profissional também não trabalhava mais na unidade.

Na mensagem, o hospital informou que aguardava a liberação de novas agendas pela coordenação médica.

Sem uma previsão de retorno, José Luiz voltou a procurar o hospital para saber quando conseguiria dar continuidade ao tratamento. A resposta foi que a unidade ainda aguardava a contratação de novos oncologistas para convocar os pacientes.

“Se não puderem me atender aqui, que me deem uma transferência para um lugar que eu possa ser atendido e resolver o meu problema, porque pra mim realmente está muito angustiante viver diariamente com a base de analgésica. É complicado”, desabafou.

Pacientes relatam meses sem quimioterapia

A situação também afeta outros pacientes que dependem do acompanhamento oncológico na unidade.

Nazaré Falcão faz tratamento contra o câncer no Hospital do Andaraí há quatro anos. Segundo ela, está há três meses sem médico e, consequentemente, sem receber quimioterapia.

“Não sei se a quimio vai continuar ou não. Estou simplesmente abandonada. Não tenho mais nada. Nem médico, nem cuidado. Nada, nada, nada”, afirmou.

A diarista Áurea Cristina também aguarda uma avaliação médica. Ela conta que teve três consultas desmarcadas e está há três meses sem conseguir passar pelo oncologista.

Segundo Áurea, o medicamento que utiliza foi prescrito por outro profissional, que forneceu receitas para um período limitado. Agora, ela teme ficar sem a medicação e não sabe quem será responsável pela continuidade do tratamento.

“Não dão explicação nenhuma. Tem três meses que eu não faço. Como é que fica agora o meu tratamento? Eu preciso passar, preciso. Urgente. Eu estou pedindo socorro”, relatou.

Prefeitura reconhece dificuldade para preencher vagas

O Hospital do Andaraí foi municipalizado há dois anos. Na época, a Prefeitura do Rio recebeu R$ 100 milhões do Ministério da Saúde para ações emergenciais na unidade.

Entre os compromissos anunciados estavam a contratação de 800 trabalhadores e a ampliação da capacidade de atendimento para 167 mil atendimentos por ano.

Procurada, a Prefeitura informou que especialistas foram contratados para o setor de oncologia, mas reconheceu que houve dificuldades para preencher todas as vagas. Segundo o município, há um edital aberto para a contratação de novos profissionais.

Um dos processos seletivos disponíveis prevê uma vaga para médico oncologista clínico, com carga horária de 12 horas. Outro edital, ainda em andamento, prevê uma vaga para oncologista clínico e outra para onco-hematologista, também com carga horária de 12 horas.

Fontes ouvidas pela reportagem apontam a terceirização como um dos fatores relacionados à falta de profissionais. Segundo esses relatos, as vagas vinculadas a organizações sociais (OSs) enfrentam dificuldades para atrair médicos, além de apresentarem maior rotatividade.

Hospital ainda não atingiu meta de leitos

Além da falta de especialistas, a estrutura de internação do Hospital do Andaraí também está abaixo da meta anunciada após a municipalização.

A previsão era de que a unidade chegasse a 450 leitos. No entanto, os números disponíveis indicam uma capacidade inferior à planejada.

De acordo com o Censo Hospitalar da Secretaria Municipal de Saúde, o hospital tinha 304 leitos em dezembro de 2024. Atualmente, são 358, mas 42 estão impedidos, ou seja, indisponíveis para uso.

A falta de médicos e a ausência de previsão para a retomada das consultas deixam pacientes oncológicos apreensivos com a continuidade dos cuidados. Para quem depende de acompanhamento regular e de medicamentos específicos, os cancelamentos sucessivos representam não apenas a espera por uma consulta, mas a incerteza sobre os próximos passos do tratamento.

A Prefeitura do Rio declarou que, desde que assumiu a gestão do Hospital do Andaraí, contratou mais de quatro mil profissionais e reabriu serviços que estavam fechados há anos.

A Prefeitura também disse que novos leitos serão abertos durante o processo de reestruturação do hospital.

Sobre os pacientes mostrados na reportagem, a Secretaria de Saúde afirmou que o atendimento deles será agendado para a próxima semana.

articles.title: Em sabatina, Vicentinho detalha alianças e afirma ter ficha limpa | G1
articles.standfirst: Na disputa pelo governo do Tocantins no segundo turno das Eleições 2026, Vicentinho Júnior (PSDB) foi o segundo candidato entrevistado pela TV Anhanguera. Confira os principais pontos da entrevista.
articles.summary: Na disputa pelo governo do Tocantins no segundo turno das Eleições 2026, Vicentinho Júnior (PSDB) foi o segundo candidato entrevistado pela TV Anhanguera.
articles.body:
No segundo turno da disputa pelo governo do Tocantins, Vicentinho Júnior (PSDB) foi o segundo candidato a ser entrevistado no Jornal Anhanguera 2ª Edição (JA2), nesta sexta-feira (16).

📱 Clique aqui para seguir o canal do g1 TO no WhatsApp

Durante a sabatina, Vicentinho Júnior apresentou propostas de modernização tecnológica para setores como saúde, meio ambiente e segurança pública, criticou o atual governo e afirmou ter certidões que comprovam sua ficha limpa diante de investigações envolvendo familiares.

Veja abaixo os principais pontos da entrevista com o Vicentinho Júnior (PSDB).

Vicentinho Júnior em entrevista ao JA2 — Foto: TV Anhanguera

O candidato abordou a consolidação de suas alianças eleitorais e destacou a adesão do atual vice-governador do estado, Laurez Moreira, à sua campanha. Ao comentar a escolha de Amélio Cayres para compor sua chapa, Vicentinho afirmou que a decisão foi baseada em critérios técnicos.

“Eu não busquei um apadrinhamento [...] eu busquei um homem que me permitisse um ambiente saudável. Que o Tocantins deseja já há algum tempo. E que haja uma sintonia entre o governador e seu vice.”

Questionado sobre eventuais interesses nas alianças recentes, o candidato declarou não ter negociado secretarias ou cargos públicos e afirmou que o objetivo é unir lideranças para atuar em prol do estado. Vicentinho negou ter recebido o apoio da ex-senadora Kátia Abreu, aliada do governo federal, e reforçou sua independência no pleito.

Em relação ao cenário nacional, Vicentinho Júnior declarou apoio ao candidato, à Presidência da República, Flávio Bolsonaro (PL). Embora Flávio tenha declarado apoio à adversária de Vicentinho na disputa pelo Palácio Araguaia, o candidato afirmou que isso não altera sua posição. “Tá tudo certo [...] Vou dar meu voto a ele porque ele é a minha melhor opção. É o projeto que eu acredito”, afirmou.

Questionado sobre a possibilidade de reeleição do presidente Lula (PT), adversário de Flávio Bolsonaro, Vicentinho afirmou que respeitará o resultado das urnas e que pretende manter o diálogo com o governo federal.

“Eu nunca pratiquei a teoria do quanto pior melhor. Eu quero que meu Brasil dê certo. Que as pautas econômicas, que os projetos sociais e que o brasileiro se encontre em uma gestão que dê certo”, disse Vicentinho.

Ao comentar as acusações sobre repasses financeiros destinados a uma empresa ligada à sua esposa, Vicentinho Júnior afirmou que foi desvinculado dos autos e que não há registros negativos contra ele. Questionado sobre a permanência do nome da esposa nas apurações, o candidato explicou que o caso envolve uma empresa distribuidora pertencente ao sogro, cujas atividades comerciais, segundo ele, são habituais e não têm relação com a esposa.

"Eu imprimo todas as minhas certidões e lancei um desafio no primeiro debate que eu fiz, Jocyelma. Vamos botar o Tocantins para ser passado a limpo. O que mais eu preciso mostrar para a minha inocência?”, perguntou o candidato.

O candidato ressaltou que não há fatos novos no processo e reafirmou que suas certidões comprovam que tem ficha limpa. Vicentinho também mencionou sua atuação na Câmara dos Deputados e disse ter se empenhado no combate à corrupção. “Eu estou há 10 meses mostrando as mesmas documentações, [...] as mesmas decisões, mas eles não se convencem”, afirmou.

Na área da saúde pública, Vicentinho Júnior criticou a gestão do setor em Araguaína e afirmou que as Unidades de Pronto Atendimento (UPAs) do município estão sobrecarregadas devido à falta de estrutura e de serviços de saúde nas cidades vizinhas de menor porte. “Uma coisa que eu deixo clara: eu não preciso perguntar a um prefeito ou a uma gestora municipal se ela me apoiou, ou não. Para celebrar [recursos]”, disse.

Como propostas, o candidato prometeu zerar as filas de espera e desafogar o atendimento no Hospital Regional de Palmas . Ele também criticou a adversária pela proximidade com o atual governo estadual e citou, como exemplo, um caso recente envolvendo a compra de medicamentos com prazo de validade vencido no estado.

“Para eles está tendo dinheiro até para comprar medicamento vencido, que falta nas estruturas oncológicas do estado do Tocantins, que falta para poder valorizar nossos servidores, terceirizados que estão sem receber... Dinheiro sempre teve. O que falta é gestão”, concluiu.

Para modernizar os serviços públicos e o setor produtivo, Vicentinho defendeu a desburocratização de processos nas áreas do agronegócio e da logística, apontando o modelo do Mato Grosso como referência para o Tocantins. A proposta inclui a reestruturação do Instituto Natureza do Tocantins (Naturatins) com o uso de ferramentas tecnológicas, além da atualização e integração dos sistemas informatizados estaduais.

A modernização também seria estendida aos serviços de saúde. "Nós temos condição de fazer por telemedicina vários dos procedimentos que hoje o Estado obriga que um cidadão, para marcar uma consulta, para fazer o primeiro atendimento, tenha que ir numa unidade de saúde", pontou.

O candidato afirmou estar alinhado ao setor de inovação e tecnologia do estado. Segundo ele, o poder público tem capacidade para avançar nessas áreas, mas a população muitas vezes não usufrui dos benefícios devido à falta de divulgação e de canais de acesso adequados. "Nós já temos os nossos notórios saberes aqui no Tocantins com condição de criar as ferramentas necessárias para facilitar a vida do cidadão e agilizar os serviços públicos", concluiu o candidato.

Ao abordar a agropecuária e a geração de empregos, Vicentinho Júnior destacou o alto custo de produção enfrentado pelos produtores locais, atribuído à escassez de operações de crédito e ao sobrepreço de insumos agrícolas essenciais.

"É estranho para um produtor rural do meu estado ficar passando a dificuldade que passa, Jocyelma, e ver uma candidata apoiada pelo atual governador, tendo ao seu lado o SEFAZ, o SEAGRO, que poderia resolver isso hoje, pedir meses de angústia e de sofrimento a um produtor do meu estado quando podia fazê-lo agora", afirmou.

Para fortalecer o setor, o candidato defendeu a recuperação e a conservação das rodovias estaduais, além da articulação com o governo federal para melhorar as ligações interestaduais. Segundo ele, a infraestrutura rodoviária e a eficiência do transporte são fundamentais para reduzir os custos de escoamento da safra e garantir a sustentabilidade da produção rural.

Na área da segurança pública e do combate à violência, Vicentinho Júnior criticou a atual administração estadual, afirmando que o governo tem se mantido ausente e em silêncio diante do avanço da criminalidade.

"O Estado tá ausente, tá calado e deixa que as facções se entendam ao invés de entrar com a altivez necessária, com a autoridade necessária para fazê-lo. Investimentos em tecnologia", disse o candidato.

Como propostas, o candidato defendeu o uso de inteligência artificial para apoiar as operações das forças de segurança. Ele também se comprometeu a convocar policiais militares aprovados em concursos públicos que aguardam nomeação. Segundo Vicentinho, o combate à criminalidade será uma das prioridades de sua gestão, caso seja eleito.

Quero agradecer a cada um dos 372.000 eleitores que foram às urnas no dia 5, deram um voto de confiança no 45. Vocês viram uma caminhada propositiva, respeitosa, altiva e constante. Continuo a ser esse candidato. Peço o voto a vocês para o nosso 45 dia, dia 25 agora de outubro, para nós fazermos um grande governo logo mais à frente", concluiu.

articles.title: Médico relata série de disparos de chumbinho que atingiram apartamento em Santos, SP | G1
articles.standfirst: Segundo o boletim de ocorrência, um dos projéteis quebrou o vidro da janela do apartamento em Santos (SP). Médico afirma temer pela segurança dos animais de estimação.
articles.summary: Segundo o boletim de ocorrência, um dos projéteis quebrou o vidro da janela do apartamento em Santos (SP). Médico afirma temer pela segurança dos animais de estimação.
articles.body:
Um médico, de 27 anos, relatou ao menos três episódios de disparos de chumbinho que atingiram o apartamento dele , em Santos , no litoral de São Paulo, desde o fim do ano passado. Segundo o boletim de ocorrência, um dos projéteis quebrou o vidro da janela , enquanto outros atingiram a persiana e a parede do prédio.

O episódio mais recente ocorreu na terça-feira (13), no bairro Boqueirão. Segundo o boletim de ocorrência, o médico afirmou ter visto um homem, que não foi identificado, em um prédio atrás de seu condomínio, subindo uma escada com um objeto parecido com uma arma.

Segundo o documento, ele também ouviu “um estampido e uma ave gritar”. O médico afirmou que, pela posição do homem, os disparos poderiam atingir o apartamento dele.

Apartamento foi atingido por tiros de chumbinho em Santos. — Foto: Arquivo Pessoal

Ainda segundo médico, ele não tem certeza de que o indivíduo seja responsável pelos disparos , mas disse que ele estava na direção de onde acredita que os projéteis tenham vindo e segurava uma espingarda de pressão.

“Não consigo afirmar com certeza que foi ele que atirou na minha janela, mas é exatamente da direção de onde vem o tiro e, por coincidência, o homem estava com uma espingarda”, relatou.

O médico teme que os disparos atinjam seus animais de estimação, já que os gatos costumam ficar na janela quando ela está aberta. “Um disparo que já foi capaz de quebrar um vidro representa um risco concreto à segurança dos moradores e dos animais”, afirmou.

Um boletim complementar foi registrado na terça-feira (13), com fotografias do homem que teria visto no prédio vizinho. Até a publicação desta reportagem ele não havia recebido resposta sobre a nova solicitação.

Em nota, a Secretaria de Segurança Pública de São Paulo (SSP-SP) informou que o caso foi registrado na Delegacia Digital e encaminhado ao 7° Distrito Policial, que realiza diligências visando a identificação do autor.

Tiro de chumbinho atingiu persiana de apartamento em Santos. — Foto: Arquivo Pessoal

articles.title: Gestante entra em trabalho de parto e filho nasce no carro em Campos | G1
articles.standfirst: Equipe do Hospital São José prestou atendimento emergencial à mãe e ao recém-nascido, que foram transferidos em seguida para o Hospital Plantadores de Cana.
articles.summary: Equipe do Hospital São José prestou atendimento emergencial à mãe e ao recém-nascido, que foram transferidos em seguida para o Hospital Plantadores de Cana.
articles.body:
Uma gestante deu à luz dentro de um carro de aplicativo enquanto estava a caminho da maternidade, em Campos dos Goytacazes , no Norte Fluminense.

Era pouco antes das 8h de quinta-feira (15) quando o motorista resolveu mudar o caminho e parou na porta do Hospital São José, pedindo ajuda. O primeiro funcionário chegou já pegando o bebê no colo.

Médicos e enfermeiros correram para ajudar a retirar a placenta e levaram a mãe e o bebê de ambulância para o Hospital Plantadores de Cana (HPC), referência em atendimento obstétrico. Os dois passam bem.

A enfermeira Marcela Gomes contou que, assim que viram que o bebê já havia nascido, se apressaram em pegar os instrumentos e realizar os procedimentos finais ali mesmo no carro.

"Quando chegamos, foi uma surpresa, porque o bebê já tinha nascido. Corremos para chamar a médica, ela cortou o cordão umbilical e esperamos o tempo adequado e seguro para a retirada da placenta. A técnica de enfermagem buscou a bandeja, montamos o campo esterilizado e preparamos o bebê para ser transferido para a maternidade", relatou a enfermeira.

A médica Sthephany Mozzer destacou que o atendimento de emergência foi conduzido de acordo com os protocolos de segurança hospitalar, com a utilização dos materiais adequados para os cuidados com a mãe e o bebê.

"A mãe iria para o HPC, mas não deu tempo, pois já estava em período expulsivo. O bebê chorou, veio com saúde. Foi tudo muito rápido. Era o quinto filho dela por parto normal", contou.

Após a conclusão dos procedimentos, a mãe e o recém-nascido foram transferidos para o Hospital Plantadores de Cana (HPC) — Foto: Hospital São José

articles.body:
Amigos se despedem do colunista Marcos Raffou em Aracaju. — Foto: Anderson Barbosa/ TV Sergipe

Amigos e familiares se despedem do colunista social Marcos Antônio Fernandes, conhecido como Marcos Raffou, nesta sexta-feira (16), em Aracaju . Ele tinha 67 anos e estava internado no Hospital de Urgências de Sergipe (Huse), onde tratava um câncer.

O velório acontece na funerária Osaf, no Centro de Aracaju e o sepultamento está marcado para as 16h, no Cemitério Santa Isabel.

Natural de São Paulo, ele se estabeleceu em Sergipe e atuou inicialmente como cabeleireiro de artistas e autoridades.

Posteriormente, como colunista social, organizou bailes da cena cultural do estado e idealizou o prêmio ‘Gente Gentíssima’, troféu que homenageava personalidades, empresas e profissionais da imprensa.

articles.title: Motociclista sofre duas paradas cardiorrespiratórias após acidente e é reanimado pelo Samu em Montes Claros | G1
articles.standfirst: Homem de 46 anos sofreu traumatismo cranioencefálico grave. Outro motociclista, de 61 anos, também ficou ferido.
articles.summary: Homem de 46 anos sofreu traumatismo cranioencefálico grave. Outro motociclista, de 61 anos, também ficou ferido.
articles.body:
Um motociclista, de 46 anos, foi reanimado duas vezes por equipes do Samu após sofrer duas paradas cardiorrespiratórias em um acidente envolvendo duas motos na tarde desta sexta-feira (16), no bairro Esplanada, em Montes Claros .

Segundo o Samu, o homem sofreu traumatismo cranioencefálico grave. Durante o atendimento, ele apresentou duas paradas cardiorrespiratórias, que foram revertidas após manobras de reanimação cardiopulmonar realizadas pela equipe médica.

Após os procedimentos, a vítima foi medicada, intubada e estabilizada. Em seguida, foi encaminhada para a Santa Casa de Montes Claros.

O outro motociclista envolvido na ocorrência tem 61 anos. Ele apresentava suspeita de fratura na clavícula e escoriações pelo corpo. Após receber os primeiros socorros, foi levado para o Hospital Universitário.

Não foram divulgados destalhes sobre a dinâmica do acidente.

articles.title: Jovem de 24 anos morre durante cirurgia plástica em hospital de Cuiabá | G1
articles.standfirst: Lurdes Maria de Lima Pessoa Padilha teve uma parada cardiorrespiratória durante os procedimentos e não resistiu, apesar de duas horas de tentativas de reanimação.
articles.summary: Lurdes Maria de Lima Pessoa Padilha teve uma parada cardiorrespiratória durante os procedimentos e não resistiu, apesar de duas horas de tentativas de reanimação.
articles.body:
Lurdes Maria de Lima Pessoa Padilha, de 24 anos — Foto: Reprodução

Uma mulher identificada como Lurdes Maria de Lima Pessoa Padilha , de 24 anos, durante a realização de cirurgias plásticas no Hospital Geral e Maternidade, em Cuiabá , nesta sexta-feira (16). A vítima sofreu uma parada cardiorrespiratória durante os procedimentos e não resistiu, apesar das tentativas de reanimação por cerca de duas horas.

Em nota, o médico Euller Gustavo Preza , responsável pelo procedimento, lamentou a morte e afirmou que a equipe identificou uma intercorrência súbita, interrompeu a cirurgia e iniciou as manobras de reanimação . Segundo o comunicado, a causa da morte deverá ser esclarecida pelos órgãos oficiais competentes.

Entre os procedimentos previstos estavam a colocação de próteses mamárias e a lipoescultura. Até o momento, não há informações confirmadas que permitam atribuir o óbito a um eventual erro médico. Lurdes era mãe de duas crianças.

Além disso, o médico informou que registrou um boletim de ocorrência após relatar ter sido agredido e ameaçado de morte. Segundo a assessoria jurídica, o registro foi feito para preservar a integridade física dele.

Por fim, ele declarou estar à disposição das autoridades e informou que n ão divulgará detalhes do atendimento em respeito à família e ao sigilo médico.

A Polícia Civil deve investigar as circunstâncias da morte.

O Dr. Euller Gustavo Preza e sua assessoria jurídica lamentam profundamente o falecimento da paciente, ocorrido nesta sexta-feira (16), e se solidarizam com a família e os amigos neste momento de dor.

O procedimento foi realizado em ambiente hospitalar adequado, por profissionais plenamente habilitados, após as avaliações pré-operatórias exigidas. Durante a cirurgia, a equipe identificou uma intercorrência súbita, interrompeu imediatamente o procedimento e manteve as manobras de reanimação por cerca de duas horas, infelizmente sem sucesso.

Tudo indica tratar-se de uma complicação súbita, descrita na literatura médica. A causa, contudo, será esclarecida pelos órgãos oficiais competentes.

O Dr. Euller tem longa trajetória e vasta experiência neste tipo de procedimento ao longo de mais de 25 anos de trabalho.

Esclarecemos que o médico regularmente inscrito no Conselho Regional de Medicina está legalmente habilitado à prática de atos médicos, inclusive cirúrgicos, nos termos da Lei nº 3.268/1957. E repudiamos veementemente quaisquer tentativas de desqualificar sua habilitação, visto que o Registro de Qualificação de Especialista (RQE) não é requisito para essa prática.

Sobre a notícia que divulga uma possível agressão ao médico, esta assessoria jurídica esclarece que tanto a agressão quanto ameaça de morte foram registradas pelo médico em um Boletim de Ocorrência, no intuito de preservar sua integridade física.

Em respeito à família e ao sigilo médico, não serão divulgadas informações do atendimento. Por isso repudiamos a divulgação indevida de imagens, de dados de prontuário ou de qualquer informação que não corresponda aos fatos.

Seguimos à inteira disposição das autoridades.

Assessoria Jurídica Alex Cardoso, OAB-MT 11.393

articles.title: Humorista Carlos Alberto de Nóbrega é internado em São Paulo para investigar possível infecção | G1
articles.standfirst: Comunicador de 90 anos está no Hospital Sírio-Libanês fazendo exames após apresentar cansaço e indisposição nos últimos meses; médicos também investigam suspeita de infecção.
articles.summary: Comunicador de 90 anos está no Hospital Sírio-Libanês fazendo exames após apresentar cansaço e indisposição nos últimos meses; médicos também investigam suspeita de infecção.
articles.body:
Carlos Alberto de Nóbrega — Foto: Globo/ Léo Rosario

O apresentador e humorista Carlos Alberto de Nóbrega, de 90 anos, está internado no Hospital Sírio-Libanês, em São Paulo , para investigar a causa de sintomas que persistem há alguns meses. Uma das hipóteses consideradas pelos médicos é a infecção pelo vírus Coxsackie .

Segundo informações divulgadas nesta sexta-feira (16), por meio das redes sociais de sua esposa, Renata de Nóbrega , o comunicador está sob os cuidados das equipes do cardiologista Roberto Kalil e do infectologista David Uip. Ele realiza exames para esclarecer o quadro de saúde e identificar a possível origem dos sintomas.

A assessoria de imprensa de Carlos Alberto confirmou ao g1 a suspeita de infecção pelo vírus Coxsackie, mas ressaltou que ainda é necessário aguardar os resultados dos exames para confirmar o diagnóstico.

Renata também passou mal, mas não precisou ficar internada e já passa bem. A assessoria de imprensa do apresentador informou ainda que, apesar de internado, ele se recupera bem.

O vírus Coxsackie pertence ao grupo dos enterovírus e pode causar diferentes tipos de infecção. Em muitos casos, provoca sintomas leves, como febre e mal-estar. Alguns tipos estão associados à doença mão-pé-boca, que pode causar feridas na boca e lesões nas mãos e nos pés. O vírus também pode provocar, em situações menos comuns, inflamações em órgãos como o coração.

articles.title: Empresário são condenados por desvio de quase meio milhão em hospital | G1
articles.standfirst: Contratos com sobrepreço e superfaturamento envolveram o Instituto Gerir e uma empresa de software; Justiça também determinou indenização por danos morais coletivos.
articles.summary: Contratos com sobrepreço e superfaturamento envolveram o Instituto Gerir e uma empresa de software; Justiça também determinou indenização por danos morais coletivos.
articles.body:
Hospital Regional Dr. José de Simone Neto — Foto: Prefeitura de Ponta Porã

Dois empresários foram condenados por desvio de recursos públicos destinados ao Hospital Regional Dr. José de Simone Neto, em Ponta Porã (MS). As irregularidades envolveram contratos firmados entre o Instituto Gerir, responsável pela administração do hospital, e uma empresa de desenvolvimento de software.

De acordo com o Ministério Público Federal (MPF), os contratos para instalação, manutenção e gestão do sistema Gestão Inteligente em Saúde (GIS) apresentavam sobrepreço e superfaturamento. O esquema teria ocorrido entre agosto de 2016 e dezembro de 2017.

Os condenados são o tesoureiro do Instituto Gerir e o sócio-administrador da empresa contratada. O primeiro recebeu pena de dois anos de reclusão, em regime aberto, além do pagamento de dez dias-multa, cada um fixado em três salários mínimos, totalizando R$ 48.630.

Já o sócio-administrador da empresa foi condenado a oito meses de reclusão, também em regime aberto, e ao pagamento de três dias-multa, cada um equivalente a cinco salários mínimos, somando R$ 24.315.

A sentença também determinou a reparação dos danos causados aos cofres públicos, estimados em R$ 476.973, e o pagamento de indenização por danos morais coletivos equivalente a três vezes o prejuízo ao erário.

O juiz federal Bruno Barbosa Stamm, da 1ª Vara Federal de Ponta Porã, considerou comprovadas a materialidade e a autoria do crime de peculato-desvio.

Entre as provas analisadas estão um relatório de auditoria elaborado pela Controladoria-Geral da União (CGU), além de e-mails e planilhas armazenados em um HD externo, que detalhavam o controle da conta-corrente utilizada no esquema.

Durante o processo, o sócio-administrador da empresa prestadora de serviços confessou ter negociado diretamente o contrato com o superintendente do Instituto Gerir.

Ele também admitiu ter elevado o valor do serviço de implantação do sistema e de seus módulos de R$ 320 mil para R$ 720 mil. O custo mensal de manutenção teria sido aumentado de R$ 12 mil para R$ 25,5 mil, com o objetivo de embutir um sobrepreço de aproximadamente 40%.

articles.standfirst: Candidato do PT percorreu o comércio do Centro da cidade e defendeu investimentos em infraestrutura e geração de empregos.
articles.summary: Cadu de Lula percorreu o comércio de Parnamirim e defendeu investimentos em infraestrutura, saúde e a geração de empregos na Grande Natal.
articles.body:
O candidato ao governo do Rio Grande do Norte Cadu de Lula (PT) fez uma caminhada nesta sexta-feira (16) pelo Centro de Parnamirim , na Grande Natal . Acompanhado de apoiadores e vereadores do município, ele ouviu reivindicações da população.

Entre as demandas apresentadas estavam melhorias na infraestrutura viária da cidade e no atendimento da rede pública estadual de saúde. Durante a agenda, Cadu citou a conclusão do Hospital Metropolitano, que está em construção, e a realização de obras para melhorar a circulação entre as regiões de Parnamirim.

"Aqui em Parnamirim vai ser o hospital metropolitano que já está sendo construído em parceria com o presidente Lula e a gente tem o compromisso de finalizar essa obra estruturante para Parnamirim, para a região metropolitana e para todo o Rio Grande do Norte. Essa cidade é dividida pela BR-101, só tem dois trechos de ligação, a gente quer fazer mais dois em parceria com o presidente Lula para integrar cada vez mais os dois lados da cidade, fazer a drenagem da Olavo Montenegro, obras que vão melhorar a vida da população de Parnamirim. A gente está falando de uma das maiores cidades do estado".

Cadu fez caminhada em Parnamirim nesta sexta — Foto: Inter TV Cabugi

O candidato também defendeu a geração de empregos por meio da industrialização do Rio Grande do Norte. Segundo ele, Parnamirim pode se consolidar como um dos polos desse desenvolvimento, aproveitando a localização e a presença de distribuidoras e fábricas no município.

"Nosso programa é um programa de desenvolvimento, geração de emprego e renda e Parnamirim está totalmente inserida nesse contexto. Aqui, a gente vai trabalhar para dar mais competitividade para as empresas virem para cá, gerar emprego e renda para o povo de Parnamirim, da Grande Natal e de todo o Rio Grande do Norte".

articles.title: Essex dad sentenced after son died in Cyprus hotel fall
articles.summary: Joshua Foster "lost control" of his son while showing him the view of a water park from a window.
articles.body:
A father whose two-year-old boy fell from a fourth floor window at a hotel in Cyprus has been fined €3,000 (£2,500) for causing his death.

Joshua Foster thought the window was closed when he placed his son on a sill to show him the view of a waterpark and "lost control" of him , Paphos District Court previously heard.

The toddler fell nearly 40ft (12.1m) at the five-star King Evelthon Beach Hotel and Resort on 12 July, the first day of the family's holiday in Chlorakas.

Foster, 37, from Essex, admitted causing death through a reckless, rash or dangerous act and was sentenced on Friday morning.

He told reporters afterwards: "Thank you for the support. I'm looking forward to going home and being with my wife and daughter."

Foster, an auditor, arrived in Cyprus hours before the incident with his wife, two children and in-laws.

They enjoyed various activities and swimming, before getting ready for dinner in the evening.

At about 18:00, Foster, his father-in-law and son were walking towards a lift when the boy noticed a waterpark outside.

Foster pushed the lift button, placed the child on the windowsill and the "inconceivable" unfolded before he could react, the court heard.

The boy was taken to Paphos General Hospital and later pronounced dead.

"The window did not appear to carry markings that would necessarily have alerted the defendant to the fact that one section was open," said District Judge Froso Christodoulidou.

His failure to establish that the window was closed led to the tragic result, the judge added.

"It was a momentary error which created a dangerous situation with fatal consequences."

The judge said there was "no evidence that the defendant deliberately exposed the child to danger", according to a translation of proceedings.

She added no sentence could outweigh the "personal consequences of the loss of his child".

In a voluntary statement to police, Foster said when he placed his son on the windowsill, the boy "fell before he had a chance to grab him".

While Foster had alcohol in his system, it did not form a significant part of the case against him - and his lawyer said there was no testimony he was drunk.

After the sentencing, Foster's lawyer, Alexandros Alexandrou, told reporters the case should have "never gone to court".

He said Foster was held in custody for eight days immediately after the incident and had to call his daughter from custody to explain what had happened.

"Within this three months, there was a lost opportunity for this man to grieve as he wanted to, to be with his family," he said.

He described his client as an "incredible father".

"[He is] an exemplary family man with a beautiful family behind him, that support him, that embraces him, that has always been by his side."

articles.title: Pope Leo's lung tumor raises questions about cancer risk for nonsmokers
articles.summary: An oncologist says Pope Leo XIV has a roughly 90% chance of cure if the lung cancer is stage 1, but pathology results will determine next steps.
articles.body: Pope Leo XIV has been diagnosed with lung cancer after a scheduled surgery, the Vatican announced Tuesday. After undergoing thoracic surgery, where surgeons removed the lower lobe of the pope’s right lung, examination of the tissue confirmed the diagnosis of lung adenocarcinoma. The diagnosis had been suspected based on testing conducted before the procedure, according to the Holy See Press Office. POPE LEO DIAGNOSED WITH LUNG CANCER AFTER SURGEONS REMOVE PART OF RIGHT LUNG, VATICAN SAYS The pope reportedly does not smoke and does not have a known history of smoking. The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention indicates that most lung cancer deaths (80%) are caused by smoking. Lung adenocarcinoma is the most common type of lung cancer, representing about 40% of all lung cancers in the U.S., according to the Lung Cancer Foundation of America. It is also the most common type among non-smokers. NEVER SMOKED A CIGARETTE? YOU COULD STILL BE AT HIGHER RISK FOR LUNG CANCER In an interview with Fox News Digital, Lary Robinson, M.D., an oncologist at Moffitt Cancer Center in Tampa, Florida, shared his surprise regarding the pope’s health status, as the lung nodule was "felt to be malignant." About 80% of lung cancers occur in people who smoke or have smoked, said Robinson, who has not treated the pope. However, he noted that lung cancer also occurs among never-smokers — including an estimated 10% of male patients and 25% of female patients. "But [the pope] had surgery and had a lobectomy, so this is usually only done with people who have localized disease, and presumably he had localized disease. And hopefully that's a stage 1 cancer," the doctor added. If the pope’s cancer is stage 1, there is a "high chance" of cure — about 90%, depending on the size of the tumor, the oncologist said. The fact that he went straight to surgery suggests there was likely no evidence that the cancer had spread. HEALTHY DIETS SPARK LUNG CANCER RISK IN NON-SMOKERS AS PESTICIDES LOOM "We'll have to wait for the pathology to determine … whether he had a stage 1 cancer and whether he needs any additional treatment afterward," Robinson said. "Size matters in lung nodules and lung cancer – the larger the cancer, the worse outlook it is, because it's more likely to be advanced and have spread." Risk factors for never-smokers Not all lung cancer cases are caused by smoking. Other factors like family history and genetic predisposition can play a role, experts say. Recent research discovered that a rare genetic mutation in the gene EGFR T790M increased lung cancer risk by 25 times compared with people who did not have the mutation, according to findings published in the journal Science. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Among people who had never smoked, carriers of the mutation had about 62 times the odds of lung cancer compared with never-smokers who were not carriers. Robinson added that other types of smoking, like pipes and cigars, can increase the risk of lung cancer, as well as heavy use of marijuana. Another risk factor is exposure to environmental toxins, such as diesel exhaust and radon, according to the oncologist. CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR HEALTH NEWSLETTER "Unfortunately, probably over half of the people who are never-smokers with lung cancer come into stage 4 disease," Robinson said. "And that's higher than people who are smokers or former smokers, so they start out at a worse stage in general." Symptoms and screening In most cases, early-stage lung cancer will not come with any symptoms, according to Robinson. In those who do have symptoms, however, the most common are related to the lungs, including a persistent cough, shortness of breath or coughing up blood. CLICK HERE FOR MORE HEALTH STORIES Unexplained weight loss can result from any form of cancer, the oncologist noted. Neurological symptoms, like persistent headaches, may also warrant seeing a doctor. Lung cancer is rare in younger adults, which is why annual CT screening is generally recommended starting at age 50 for those at high risk, the doctor said. People considered at high risk include current smokers with at least a 20 pack-year history, as well as former smokers who quit within the past 15 years. TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ "Only about 15% of the people who are eligible get screened, unfortunately," Robinson said. "I'm hoping that within four or five years, a screening CT scan will only be confirmatory after they have a positive blood test done at your doctor's office." That approach could make screening easier and potentially help detect more lung cancers, according to the doctor.

articles.title: This Is the No. 1 Risk Factor for Dementia That You Can Actually Prevent, According to a Geriatrician
articles.summary: As we get older, the world gradually starts looking and sounding a little different.
articles.body: As we get older, the world gradually starts looking and sounding a little different. Our vision may not be as sharp as it once was, and we may need to hit the “increase volume” button on the remote a few extra times to hear the television. Most people will experience some degree of age-related hearing loss, which usually becomes more apparent over the age of 60, Dr. Stephanie Rogers, a professor of medicine in the division of geriatrics at the University of California San Francisco School of Medicine, tells TODAY.com. However, hearing problems can begin even earlier in life. And leaving them unaddressed may seriously impact the brain, increasing the risk of cognitive decline, says Rogers. Longevity Tip of the Day: Address Hearing Loss to Lower Your Risk of Developing Dementia Untreated hearing loss is the No. 1 modifiable risk factor for dementia, says Rogers. Modifiable risk factors are behaviors or exposures that can influence our risk of developing a disease. Unlike non-modifiable risk factors, such as our genetics, these can be changed. Hearing loss typically begins subtly in early adulthood and slowly accrues over decades. “Loud noise damage can start to occur in your teens and 20s,” says Rogers. If you experience noticeable hearing changes or problems during mid-life, it’s time to get checked out. People who develop hearing loss between the ages of 40-65 may have a greater risk for developing dementia, according to the Alzheimer’s Society. Dementia refers to a group of symptoms that affect memory, speech and social abilities. It affects at least 7 million Americans. Why It Matters Hearing loss can increase the risk of dementia in a few different ways, Rogers says. First, it puts a huge cognitive load on the brain. “When one can’t hear as well, the brain expends a lot of energy trying to decode speech. This depletes the reserve available for other cognitive tasks, like the encoding of memories or memory consolidation,” says Rogers. The reduced auditory input may also cause certain parts of the brain to atrophy or weaken because they aren’t being used as much anymore, says Rogers. Sensory deprivation can also reduce neuroplasticity, or our brain’s ability to adapt and rewire itself. Finally, hearing loss can contribute to social isolation, which is another major risk factor for dementia. “Many people who can’t hear as well start to not participate in conversations or social situations,” says Rogers. It can cause an otherwise outgoing, bubbly person to become more withdrawn. Fortunately, hearing loss can be addressed to help reduce the risk of dementia, Rogers says. How To Get Started First, it’s important to recognize the symptoms of hearing loss. “Usually the first sign is difficulty understanding speech when there is background noise, i.e. in a restaurant,” says Rogers. Sounds may become muffled, you may find yourself asking people to repeat themselves, or needing to turn the radio or television volume higher, per the Mayo Clinic. If you’re experiencing any of these issues, talk to your doctor. They may refer you to a specialist for further testing. “I use the American Academy of Otolaryngology-Head and Neck surgery guidelines for hearing loss screening,” says Rogers. “Everyone should get screening, whether you notice hearing loss or not, at age 50, then every three to five years until age 65, then every one to three years after age 65,” Rogers adds. Hearing aids are a first-line treatment for age-related hearing loss. “There are over-the-counter versions for patients with mild-to-moderate loss, which can help the majority of people. There are also prescription hearing aids for more severe hearing loss,” Rogers adds. In addition to addressing hearing loss, Rogers recommends other lifestyle habits to promote brain and heart health, which may reduce dementia risk. “Things like controlling cholesterol, blood sugar, blood pressure ... not smoking and avoiding excessive alcohol intake, and consistent exercise are also important.” TODAY’s Expert Tip of the Day series is all about simple strategies to make life a little easier. Every Monday through Friday, different qualified experts share their best advice on diet, fitness, heart health, mental wellness and more.

articles.title: ‘Dowry murder’: Woman’s body cremated at in-laws’ doorstep
articles.summary: Muzaffarpur: 19-year-old married woman found dead; family alleges dowry murder, names husband and in-laws. Body cremated at in-laws’ doorstep; probe on.
articles.body: Patna: A newly married woman was found dead at her house in Rajwara Dih village under Mushahari police station area in Muzaffarpur district on Wednesday night, following which her family alleged murder. Her relatives later cremated the body of Gunja Kumari, 19, at her in-laws’ doorstep on Thursday evening.Gunja’s family has accused four people, including her husband Kundan Kumar, of murdering her over dowry. Kundan, his brother Chandan Paswan and other in-laws are absconding. Police have registered a case based on the family’s application and started an investigation.Gunja’s maternal uncle Chhotu Kumar said a ward member of Rajwara village informed him about her death. Her family reached Rajwara Dih from Kanti around midnight on Wednesday and found the body lying in a room with marks on her neck. Police reached the spot, pacified the family and sent the body to SKMCH for post-mortem.Chhotu said Gunja and Kundan met during the Rudra Mahayagya in Simraha Chaturbhuj village near Jhapahan in 2024. They fell in love, eloped and married. The families later agreed to their marriage, following which they were married again according to Hindu rituals.Gunja’s grandmother Siya Janki Devi alleged Kundan had been torturing her for dowry since their marriage. She said the family was preparing to give dowry items on Dhanteras, but Gunja died before that.According to Chhotu, Gunja had returned to her maternal home around three months ago and was brought back after a panchayat decision.In the FIR, the family has accused Kundan, Chandan, Priyanka Devi and Sulekha Devi of murder.Mushahari SHO Subodh Kumar Mehta said, “After the death of the married woman, police had reached the spot on information of ruckus. People were pacified and the body was sent for post-mortem.”Mehta said police later learned about the cremation at the in-laws’ doorstep. “Action will be taken in this matter also. articles.title: Trump administration advances plan for peptide drugs favored by RFK Jr.
articles.summary: Health officials are moving ahead with a plan to allow compounding pharmacies to make certain peptides including BPC-157.
articles.body: U.S. health officials are moving ahead with a plan to allow specialty pharmacies to produce certain peptides, a class of largely unregulated injections that have become popular among followers of Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. and other wellness influencers. Kennedy’s Department of Health and Human Services submitted a peptides “interim access policy” to the White House for review, according to a posting Thursday on a government website. The plan was sent to the Office of Management and Budget, which reviews federal rules and regulations with the potential for significant economic impact. HHS officials did not immediately respond to requests for comment Thursday afternoon. Peptides are the building blocks of more complex proteins, triggering hormones inside the body needed for growth, metabolism and healing. Drug companies have brought several to market as medications, including mainstay treatments for diabetes and weight loss. But the ones at issue here haven’t gone through that rigorous vetting process. Nevertheless, they have gained a foothold among Americans interested in bulking up, looking younger or boosting energy. Those uses are not approved by the Food and Drug Administration and most of the data on peptides comes from animal studies. Before joining the administration, Kennedy publicly declared that “FDA’s war” on peptides and other wellness products would soon end. After becoming health secretary, Kennedy said U.S. compounding pharmacies must be allowed to sell peptides because Americans were increasingly turning to “gray market” peptides made in China and other countries. Those products remain widely available for purchase via online platforms like TikTok. The White House filing doesn’t give specifics of the new policy, but two people familiar with the plan say it is intended to allow pharmacies to temporarily compound some of the most popular peptides, including BPC-157, a chemical promoted to build muscle and heal injuries. The people spoke on condition of anonymity to discuss confidential government deliberations. The update is the latest indication that Kennedy and other Trump administration officials are looking to ease access to unproven products that are popular within the Make America Healthy Again movement. Some of the biggest MAHA figures sell peptide injections and supplements. The FDA previously placed BPC-157 and more than a dozen other injectable peptides on its list of substances that are too risky to be compounded by pharmacies. Possible risks include contamination, allergic reactions and tumor growth, according to the FDA. But earlier this year, Kennedy directed the agency to reconsider a short list of chemicals that have been widely promoted by wellness influencers and fitness celebrities. In July, a panel of external FDA advisers recommended the agency drop its restrictions on six of the seven peptides put before them. That recommendation went against the scientific conclusion of FDA’s staff scientists, who reiterated that none of the peptides had been studied enough to establish their safety and effectiveness. The new policy sent to the White House would essentially assure compounding pharmacies — specialty businesses that mix customized medications that aren’t available from traditional drugmakers — that they won’t be targeted for producing certain peptides, according to the people familiar with the plan. That approach, known as enforcement discretion, allows the FDA to selectively choose to not enforce some of its own regulations. Formally adding the peptides to FDA’s list of drugs that are safe for compounding would require federal rulemaking, a process that could take years and involves multiple rounds of public comment. It was not immediately clear if the administration still plans to pursue that process. The proposal was quickly praised online by some Kennedy allies who sell peptides. “This is huge,” Brigham Buhler, a wellness clinic operator who sells peptides through an online service, posted on X. “This isn’t about whether you’re for or against peptides. It’s about whether you’re for or against MEDICAL FREEDOM.” The panel of outside experts that met in July was selected by Kennedy’s health department and included several doctors, pharmacists and consultants who work in the peptide field. The peptide business has caught the attention of major telehealth providers, including Hims & Hers and Noom. Both companies recently announced plans to offer peptides to their customers if the federal government eases access. Wall Street analysts estimate the market could be worth $2 billion to $3 billion.

articles.title: Pope pictured for first time since surgery and cancer diagnosis
articles.summary: The pontiff was diagnosed with lung cancer after having surgery at Rome's Gemelli Hospital on Tuesday.
articles.body:
Pope Leo XIV has been pictured celebrating Mass from hospital, in the first images of him released by the Vatican since he underwent lung surgery.

The 71-year-old pontiff was diagnosed with lung cancer after the surgery at Rome's Gemelli Hospital on Tuesday afternoon, which the Vatican said had been "successful" and proceeded without complications.

The images shared on Friday showed the Chicago-born Pope wearing a green robe while standing behind a makeshift altar on the tenth floor of the hospital.

Pope Leo "celebrated with the medical and nursing staff" and thanked workers for their service, the Vatican press office said.

Pope's cancer diagnosis leaves Catholics questioning what comes next

On Friday, the Pope's doctors said tests had shown "a steady improvement in his general condition" since his procedure.

His doctors said that a chest X-ray indicated "good recovery of the operated lung".

The whole lower lobe of the Pope's right lung was removed "to ensure the procedure was radical", the Vatican said following the surgery.

"After the operation, the Pope awoke normally and returned after a brief period of observation to his room," it said earlier, before he spent a "peaceful night" at the hospital.

Pope Leo first announced that he would be having the operation during his weekly Sunday prayers, telling the crowd in St Peter's Square that doctors had found a "well-contained" nodule on his lung "at an early stage" and advised him to have it removed.

Nodules are quite common and not necessarily cancerous, but after it was examined the medical team confirmed it was, "as suspected by pre-operative tests", the Vatican said. He was diagnosed with lung adenocarcinoma.

The Vatican has stressed that the Pope had shown no symptoms of infection or illness prior to the procedure.

articles.title: I lost half my right lung to cancer. Pope Leo's diagnosis gives me hope
articles.summary: A lung cancer survivor compares her stage 1B diagnosis and surgery to Pope Leo's adenocarcinoma, urging expanded screening beyond heavy smokers.
articles.body: When Pope Leo told the crowd in St. Peter's Square on Sunday that doctors had found "a small, localized nodule" in his lung, the reassurances came fast. Most nodules are benign, media medical experts quickly said. Probably nothing to worry about. I heard the same reassurances about my own lung not long ago. They were wrong then, and on Tuesday the Vatican confirmed they were wrong now. The nodule was adenocarcinoma, lung cancer. Surgeons removed the lower lobe of the Holy Father's right lung through a few small incisions, guided by a camera rather than an open chest, and he was back in his room the same afternoon. POPE LEO DIAGNOSED WITH LUNG CANCER AFTER SURGEONS REMOVE PART OF RIGHT LUNG, VATICAN SAYS That is almost exactly what happened to me. Half of my right lung was removed just 12 months ago, and I was running just four weeks after that. So, my first reaction when I heard the pope's diagnosis was not dread. It was hope. I was 43, a mother of four, a daily runner, and the daughter of a lung doctor. The morning I learned I had lung cancer, I had already completed a six-mile run without a hint that anything was wrong. I had no symptoms. Under current guidelines, I was not supposed to be at risk, and I did not qualify for screening. POPE LEO UNDERGOES BLOOD TESTS, X-RAY FOLLOWING CANCER SURGERY, VATICAN SAYS My diagnosis came from a scan I chose, not from a symptom. My husband and I have always leaned toward proactive testing, and at his urging I scheduled what I assumed would be a baseline full-body scan, paid for out of pocket. It showed a 3.8-centimeter nodule on my right lung. Initial advice from the reading radiologist recommended to follow-up if symptoms occurred. But with a father as a lung doctor and a friend as a lung radiologist, they pushed me to follow up sooner. The new low dose CT of my chest showed the mass had grown in just two months. But that scan led to a diagnosis of stage 1B lung cancer and, like the pope, to surgery to remove it. Still, no symptoms ever appeared. Four weeks to the day after my operation, I was on a plane. I was running again within weeks. Caught early and handled by a skilled medical team and a surgeon who does this every day, lung cancer is not a death sentence. It is a survivable disease, a fixable problem. If the pope keeps his November trip to South America, he will board that plane about as far out from surgery as I was. DR MARC SIEGEL: POPE LEO'S LUNG SURGERY PUTS MODERN MEDICINE ALONGSIDE FAITH So the gloom I see in my text threads with Catholic friends this week is misplaced. What should worry Americans is something else entirely. The pope's cancer was found during a routine checkup. Mine was found because I paid for a scan no one recommended. Most Americans get neither. Lung cancer is the leading cause of cancer death in the United States and one of the most expensive cancers to treat, because it is usually found late. Current guidelines recommend screening only for adults ages 50 to 80 with a heavy smoking history. Fewer than one in five people who qualify ever get the scan. And nearly two-thirds of people diagnosed with lung cancer would not have qualified at all. I am one of them. POPE LEO'S LUNG TUMOR RAISES QUESTIONS ABOUT CANCER RISK FOR NONSMOKERS Stage at diagnosis is the strongest predictor of both survival and cost. Found at stage I, five-year survival can exceed 90%. Yet most cases are still found after the disease has spread, when curative treatment becomes unlikely. There is a fix on the table. The Saving Health by Identifying Risk for Americans (SHIRA) Act, a draft bill now circulating in the White House, HHS and Congress, would make lung cancer screening free to the patient under Medicare — no copay, no deductible. It would cover veterans exposed to burn pits, guarantee a first scan to cancer survivors and those with a family history, and require Medicare to modernize who counts as "high risk" so that never-smokers, like me, stop being invisible. It builds a path toward age-based screening after 40, the way we already screen for breast and colorectal cancer. CLICK HERE FOR MORE FOX NEWS OPINION I was fortunate. A preventive scan, a persistent friend and father, and an early diagnosis gave me a future I might not otherwise have had. The pope was fortunate too: a routine check found his cancer before he felt a thing. Luck should not decide who survives lung cancer. Screening policy should. articles.title: Mom, 31, Recalls ‘Unbearable’ Colon Cancer Symptom That Doctor Dismissed in Pregnancy
articles.summary: A pregnant mom went to the hospital repeatedly for painful acid reflux, but doctors reassured her it was normal. The root cause turned out to be colon cancer.
articles.body: When Geraldine Levano, 31, was pregnant with her second son, the acid reflux didn’t alarm her. But it got to a point where “I couldn’t even take the pain,” Levano of Houston, Texas, tells TODAY.com. Working as a medical assistant, she asked her co-workers and OB-GYN if her reflux was normal. “And of course they’re like ... it’s just the baby, you’re fine,” Levano recalls. A few times when the pain became “unbearable,” she went to the hospital. But they just reassured her that her baby looked totally healthy and her symptoms were normal during pregnancy. Medication didn’t do much. “Nothing would help,” she says. “It just felt like like a burning sensation with pain, and I just felt like something was stuck there.” So she toughed it out until early April 2022, about two weeks after her son was born, when she felt a painful lump right under her ribcage on her left side. And he was still having reflux. She ended up seeing the doctor whose office she works in now, who ordered an ultrasound. What should have been a 15-minute appointment quickly turned into an hourslong ordeal as it became clear the doctors needed more imaging. The next day, her pain went from a 10 to a 20, Levano recalls. “I couldn’t even walk,” she says, “I couldn’t even carry my baby, so I went to the hospital.” Before they even took her vitals, the doctor took a look at her ultrasound and said, “You have cancer. We just need to figure out where,” Levano recalls. Testing Revealed Stage 3 Colorectal Cancer After a CT scan, Levano was told her cancer was in her colon. That imaging revealed a large mass, about 8 centimeters, that was nearly obstructing her colon, Dr. Amit Agarwal, professor and colorectal surgeon with UTHealth Houston and Memorial Hermann Hospital, tells TODAY.com. He also saw that her tumor was putting pressure on her stomach, which explained Levano’s acid reflux. “The mass was actually pushing up on the stomach from behind it,” explains Agarwal, who was Levano’s surgeon. “Everything that she would eat was not necessarily being digested, so the acid would come back up.” While acid reflux is a common and normal symptom during pregnancy, he says, it should not continue after pregnancy. Looking back, Levano says she’d also lost weight, which she’d attributed to nausea, and had “always suffered with constipation,” which could have also been signs of the cancer. Agarwal notes that she was also anemic, another symptom that could have easily been attributed to her pregnancy or colon cancer. “But after pregnancy, when you still continue to have those things, that’s when the light bulb goes off,” he says. Having previously worked for a gastroenterologist, Levano was able to get a colonoscopy the following week. But because the mass in her colon was so large, “he was too afraid to be able to go all the way in,” she says. The tumor “was blocking pretty much my whole colon,” she adds. So, she met with Agarwal to decide on her next steps. Because of the size of the mass and the near-total obstruction it was causing, Agarwal knew that Levano needed surgery before chemotherapy. Surgery Followed by Months of Treatment Her surgery was scheduled about two weeks later, and she woke up from it with a surprise: a colostomy bag, which collects waste from the colon. Agarwal had told her there was a chance she might need one, she says, but he wouldn’t be sure until he did the surgery. Of course, she had hoped it wouldn’t be necessary, but that wasn’t how things went. “Anytime you get chemotherapy, you weaken the tissue,” Agarwal explains. So, if he had reconnected her colon during that surgery, the chemotherapy she was going to receive afterward could have either broken down the connection or narrowed it, causing a bowel obstruction. For safety purposes, Agarwal decided to give her the temporary colostomy bag and wait until after she went through chemotherapy to repair her colon. It was an added challenge for Levano, who spent the next few months going through chemotherapy before having the bag removed in December that year. Around that same time, her mom was diagnosed with endometrial cancer, adding another layer to an emotional time. Levano was trying to balance “a newborn baby, a 3-year-old baby, and then my mom trying to be a mom to me, and me trying to be a mom to my own kids,” she says. “It was very, very hard.” The chemo often left her feeling fatigued and nauseous, with neuropathic pain in her hands and legs that made it tough to even walk. During that time, she leaned on her family for help, including her husband and dad. And her sister “was pretty much a second mom to my kids for a while,” Levano says. After chemotherapy, she underwent immunotherapy. Compared to chemo, the immunotherapy side effects were “minimal,” Levano says. And in August of 2023, she rang the bell to celebrate the end of her treatment. A Surprise Lynch Syndrome Diagnosis Today, Levano is celebrating more than three years in remission and doing “really good,” she says, adding that she just had a clean colonoscopy and endoscopy. Mentally and emotionally, however, she is still grappling with her experience. “It does break my heart,” Levano says, to see so many people out there with cancer, especially young people, who haven’t had treatment as successful as hers. “I’ll never question God, and I’m so grateful that I’m still here,” she says, “but then it hurts me for the people that are still going through it or that don’t make it.” The weight of wondering why her cancer was treated while others aren’t so lucky takes a toll, she says. Her recovery was complicated by a diagnosis of Lynch syndrome, a genetic condition that increases the risk for certain types of cancer — particularly colon and uterine cancer — at a young age. So, after her colon cancer experience, she decided to have a partial hysterectomy. And she’ll continue to get additional yearly screenings, including colonoscopies. “Yes, the prep is disgusting,” she says. “But at the end of the day, if it can save you, do it.” The idea that she may have passed this genetic risk onto her sons, now 4 and 7, has caused her some anxiety about their health. “Any little sickness, any little pain that they’re having, I was taking them to the hospital,” she says. Since then, she’s “relaxed a little bit,” she says, “but to this day, it still affects me.” Ultimately, Levano hopes her story inspires others to advocate for themselves when something feels off. “If you feel like something is wrong, never take no for an answer,” she says.

articles.title: Pope Leo XIV seen for first time since lung cancer surgery amid major recovery milestone
articles.summary: The Vatican released first photos of Pope Leo XIV celebrating mass at Gemelli Hospital, days after surgeons removed a lung lobe due to adenocarcinoma.
articles.body: Pope Leo XIV is up and moving after having part of his lung removed. After undergoing thoracic surgery Tuesday, during which surgeons removed the lower lobe of the pope’s right lung, examination of the tissue confirmed a diagnosis of lung adenocarcinoma, or lung cancer, according to the Vatican. The pope, 71, has spent four days recovering at Gemelli Hospital in Rome, Italy, after the successful procedure. DR MARC SIEGEL: POPE LEO'S LUNG SURGERY PUTS MODERN MEDICINE ALONGSIDE FAITH On Friday, the Vatican released the first photos of Pope Leo after the operation. The pope is pictured standing at an altar in green vestments, celebrating Mass in a makeshift chapel at the hospital where he distributed communion. According to a Holy See Press Office statement, several members of Gemelli’s medical and nursing staff and members of the Vatican City State Gendarmerie Corps attended the service. POPE LEO'S LUNG TUMOR RAISES QUESTIONS ABOUT CANCER RISK FOR NONSMOKERS "In his homily, the pope thanked all the staff — doctors, nurses and orderlies — for the work they do every day caring for patients in their frailty and especially for what they have done and continue to do for him," the statement said. The Vatican also confirmed on Friday that the pope’s recovery continues with "steady improvement in his overall condition." Dr. Luigi Carbone and professor Stefano Margaritora added that the pope’s "post-operative recovery allows him to carry out normal daily activities entirely independently." Pope Leo plans to make his first public appearance since the procedure on Sunday during the noon Angelus, which he normally leads. NEVER SMOKED A CIGARETTE? YOU COULD STILL BE AT HIGHER RISK FOR LUNG CANCER Fox News senior medical analyst Dr. Marc Siegel said the pope’s procedure included a small incision with VAT (video-assisted thoracoscopy), which involves less pain and has a quicker recovery. The pope has been in good health "to begin with" and is highly active, which plays a "major role in recovery," Siegel told Fox News Digital. "Since he wasn’t a smoker and likely had very good underlying lung function, loss of a lobe, when there are three total on the right, shouldn’t have a major impact on daily activity, especially with pain controlled," the doctor added. CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR HEALTH NEWSLETTER In a separate Fox News Digital interview, Lary Robinson, an oncologist at Moffitt Cancer Center in Tampa, Florida, shared his surprise regarding the pope’s health status. About 80% of lung cancers occur in people who smoke or have smoked, said Robinson, who has not treated the pope. However, he noted that lung cancer also occurs among never-smokers, including an estimated 10% of male patients and 25% of female patients. CLICK HERE FOR MORE HEALTH STORIES "But [the pope] had surgery and had a lobectomy, so this is usually only done with people who have localized disease, and presumably he had localized disease. And hopefully that's a Stage 1 cancer," the doctor added. If the pope’s cancer is Stage 1, there is a "high chance" of cure — about 90% — depending on the size of the tumor, the oncologist said. The fact that he went straight to surgery suggests there was likely no evidence that the cancer had spread. TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ "We'll have to wait for the pathology to determine … whether he needs any additional treatment afterward," Robinson said. articles.title: While bereaved family waited for body, Maharashtra doctor held liquor party at autopsy department
articles.summary: Pune YCMH doctor suspended after video shows alleged liquor party in postmortem department; inquiry ordered amid claims of bribes to release bodies.
articles.body: PUNE: The Yashwantrao Chavan Memorial Hospital (YCMH) has been rocked by a third controversy in a month, and second in only a week, after a video surfaced showing a senior doctor holding a liquor party in the postmortem department. Pimpri Chinchwad municipal commissioner Vijay Suryawanshi has suspended the doctor in question, medical officer Dr Vaibhav Mhaske.In the past five weeks, two viral videos have sparked a firestorm of criticism against YCMH. The most recent video showed a homeless patient and the stretcher he was strapped to falling out of a moving ambulance. An earlier video showed a raucous dhol-tasha performance on the hospital’s premises on Sept 22.In Friday’s suspension order, Suryawanshi stated that Mhaske was found intoxicated while on duty and disrupted essential services, such as patient care, surgeries and other critical hospital services.The action follows the circulation of a video reportedly recorded on Oct 3, when a daily-wage worker from Dharashiv district suffered an accident on a construction site in Thergaon and was brought to YCMH, where he was pronounced dead on arrival.The video shows the family of the deceased requesting an apparently intoxicated Mhaske to release the documents required to claim the body. A bottle of liquor is visible on a table beside him.One person who claimed to be a friend of the deceased, told TOI that the video was recorded after the family was made to wait overnight to receive the body. The man also alleged that hospital staff demanded a payment to immediately release the body.“When the family approached the postmortem department for the necessary documents, they were told the body would be handed over only in the morning. If they wanted it at night, they would have to pay,” he alleged.The video has since been circulated widely on social media, triggering demands for strict action.Activist Maruti Bhapkar said the incident had tarnished the hospital’s image and called for a detailed investigation. “The staff involved should be dismissed from service to send a clear message that such conduct will not be tolerated,” he said.The video has shifted focus on the alleged demands for payment to release bodies at night, with several social media users sharing similar experiences.
