articles.title: TDAH e autismo: o que explica o aumento recorde de diagnósticos? | G1
articles.standfirst: Revisão independente mostra que problemas de saúde mental passaram a atingir um em cada quatro jovens de 16 a 24 anos. Especialistas alertam para subdiagnóstico, dificuldades de acesso ao tratamento e riscos do uso de inteligência artificial na assistência.
articles.summary: Revisão alerta que o aumento nos diagnósticos de TDAH e autismo convive com o subdiagnóstico e a falta de acesso ao tratamento para jovens.
articles.body:
Mais diagnósticos significam mais casos? O que os dados sobre TDAH e autismo conseguem mostrar — Foto: Adobe Stock

A proporção de jovens de 16 a 24 anos com transtornos mentais comuns aumentou significativamente nas últimas três décadas no Reino Unido. Em 1993, aproximadamente um em cada seis jovens apresentava essas condições. Em 2024, a proporção chegou a um em cada quatro. Ao mesmo tempo, os diagnósticos registrados de autismo e transtorno de déficit de atenção e hiperatividade (TDAH) cresceram mais de 20 e seis vezes, respectivamente, em determinadas faixas etárias.

Os dados fazem parte de uma revisão independente sobre saúde mental, autismo e TDAH, liderada pelo professor Peter Fonagy, publicada na última sexta-feira (9). O relatório analisa o aumento dos problemas de saúde mental, as mudanças nos diagnósticos e os desafios enfrentados pelos serviços de atendimento no Reino Unido.

Entre os principais resultados e avaliações destacados por especialistas estão:

Aumento dos transtornos mentais: enquanto problemas relacionados à ansiedade, preocupação, pensamentos depressivos e pânico se tornaram mais frequentes entre os jovens, a irritabilidade diminuiu e os problemas de conduta permaneceram estáveis.

Crescimento dos diagnósticos de autismo e TDAH: os registros aumentaram, respectivamente, mais de 20 vezes e mais de seis vezes em determinadas faixas etárias . Especialistas lembram que essas condições foram historicamente subdiagnosticadas, deixando muitas pessoas sem identificação adequada durante anos.

Excesso ou falta de diagnósticos: pesquisadores afirmam que as duas situações podem ocorrer simultaneamente. O crescimento dos registros não significa necessariamente que todas as pessoas que precisam de atendimento estejam sendo identificadas.

Dificuldade de acesso ao tratamento: dados do Escritório Nacional de Auditoria britânico indicam que apenas cerca de um quarto das crianças com provável condição de saúde mental consegue acessar serviços financiados pelo Serviço Nacional de Saúde (NHS).

Risco de restringir atendimento: especialistas alertam que priorizar apenas pacientes com dificuldades mais graves pode deixar sem assistência pessoas autistas ou com TDAH cujas necessidades são menos evidentes.

Inteligência artificial na saúde mental: ferramentas digitais podem contribuir para o atendimento, mas não devem substituir profissionais de saúde, especialmente em situações de risco.

A principal recomendação da revisão é uma mudança na maneira como os serviços de saúde, educação e assistência social oferecem ajuda. Em vez de depender exclusivamente de diagnósticos formais, o sistema deveria considerar as necessidades individuais e permitir que as pessoas recebam apoio mais rapidamente.

A proposta recebeu avaliações positivas de especialistas ouvidos pelo Science Media Centre, organização britânica independente que reúne comentários científicos sobre temas de interesse público. Mas os pesquisadores ressaltam que a mudança dependerá da ampliação dos serviços e da disponibilidade de profissionais qualificados.

Especialistas ouvidos pelo g1 explicam que o crescimento dos registros está relacionado a fatores como maior conscientização, mudanças nos critérios diagnósticos e identificação de pessoas que anteriormente passavam despercebidas pelos serviços de saúde.

O psiquiatra de crianças e adolescentes e professor de psiquiatria da Universidade de São Paulo (USP) Guilherme Polanczyk afirma que há um aumento dos diagnósticos de transtornos mentais, incluindo autismo e TDAH, em todo o mundo. Alguns estudos de prevalência também sugerem um crescimento do número de pessoas afetadas, mas as pesquisas nesse sentido ainda são mais limitadas.

O neurologista infantil Felipe Kalil, professor da Escola de Medicina da PUC-RS e coordenador do Serviço de Neurologia Infantil do Hospital Moinhos de Vento, acrescenta que os avanços na capacidade de identificar essas condições ajudam a explicar parte do crescimento observado.

Para os especialistas, a questão central não é simplesmente descobrir se existem diagnósticos demais ou de menos, mas entender quem realmente apresenta essas condições, quem está sendo identificado corretamente e quantas pessoas continuam sem acesso ao acompanhamento necessário.

Aumento dos transtornos mentais entre jovens é real, dizem pesquisadores

Um dos pontos centrais da revisão é a constatação de que o crescimento dos problemas de saúde mental entre jovens não pode ser explicado apenas por uma maior disposição das pessoas para falar sobre seus sintomas.

O aumento, entretanto, não ocorreu de maneira uniforme entre os diferentes sintomas e comportamentos.

Problemas relacionados à preocupação, ansiedade, pensamentos depressivos e pânico se tornaram mais frequentes. Por outro lado, a irritabilidade diminuiu, enquanto os problemas de conduta permaneceram estáveis.

Uma pessoa pode apresentar sofrimento emocional sem necessariamente preencher os critérios clínicos para um transtorno mental. Da mesma forma, alguém pode precisar de apoio mesmo sem ter recebido um diagnóstico formal.

Diagnósticos de autismo e TDAH cresceram mais de 20 e seis vezes

Outro ponto de destaque da revisão é o crescimento expressivo dos diagnósticos registrados de autismo e TDAH.

Em alguns grupos, o número de diagnósticos registrados já se aproxima ou ultrapassa as estimativas de prevalência dessas condições na população.

O cenário alimenta discussões sobre a possibilidade de diagnósticos excessivos. No entanto, os pesquisadores ressaltam que o aumento dos registros não significa, necessariamente, que mais pessoas estejam recebendo diagnósticos indevidos.

Polanczyk explicou ao g1 que, embora o crescimento dos diagnósticos seja evidente, ainda não está claro se houve um aumento proporcional do número de pessoas afetadas na população.

“Hoje, quando a gente faz diagnóstico, a gente está fazendo com outros critérios que de fato inclui um número que inclui pessoas com habilidades e dificuldades mais leves do que no passado”, explica.

Por isso, comparar o aumento dos diagnósticos registrados com estimativas consideradas estáveis pode produzir uma interpretação equivocada sobre a existência de diagnósticos excessivos.

O que mudou na forma de diagnosticar autismo e TDAH?

Uma das principais explicações para o aumento dos diagnósticos está na transformação dos critérios utilizados para reconhecer essas condições.

Polanczyk explica que, no caso do autismo, uma mudança importante ocorreu em 2013, com a publicação da quinta edição do Manual Diagnóstico e Estatístico de Transtornos Mentais (DSM-5).

A partir dessa atualização, passou-se a adotar uma compreensão mais ampla do transtorno do espectro autista (TEA), incluindo pessoas com alterações na comunicação e padrões de comportamento rígidos ou repetitivos que apresentam manifestações menos intensas.

Na prática, isso significa que pessoas que anteriormente não preenchiam os critérios para receber o diagnóstico passaram a ser reconhecidas dentro do espectro.

“No momento em que a gente muda a forma de diagnosticar o autismo, é difícil comparar as taxas de hoje com as taxas do passado. Mas, sem dúvida, o número de diagnósticos aumentou”, afirma Polanczyk.

O avanço das estratégias de triagem, a maior conscientização da população e a ampliação do acesso aos serviços de saúde também contribuíram para que crianças e adolescentes que antes poderiam passar anos sem diagnóstico fossem identificados.

Isso, porém, não exclui completamente a possibilidade de um crescimento real da prevalência.

“É possível que exista também algum aumento real relacionado a fatores genéticos e ambientais. Portanto, o crescimento observado nos diagnósticos provavelmente reflete uma combinação de melhora da triagem, maior acesso aos serviços de saúde e reconhecimento mais precoce”, acrescenta Kalil.

Há excesso de diagnósticos ou pessoas sem atendimento?

Os especialistas ressaltam que o excesso e a falta de diagnósticos não são situações necessariamente excludentes. Ambas podem ocorrer simultaneamente, inclusive dentro de um mesmo sistema de saúde.

No caso de autismo e TDAH, o crescimento dos registros levanta questionamentos sobre a relação entre diagnósticos e necessidades clínicas. Já em condições como ansiedade e depressão, muitas pessoas continuam sem identificação e assistência especializada.

Polanczyk afirma que é possível encontrar contextos específicos em que os diagnósticos e os tratamentos superam as estimativas de prevalência.

Ele cita estudos realizados nos Estados Unidos que identificaram taxas de uso de medicamentos estimulantes superiores à prevalência estimada de TDAH em determinados grupos.

Esses resultados podem indicar situações de diagnóstico ou tratamento excessivo. Entretanto, o psiquiatra ressalta que esse cenário não representa necessariamente a realidade da população como um todo.

No Brasil, por exemplo, as desigualdades de acesso aos serviços especializados são um obstáculo importante.

Segundo Polanczyk, estimativas produzidas por seu grupo de pesquisa em São Paulo e Porto Alegre, há cerca de cinco anos, apontaram que aproximadamente 80% dos adolescentes com diagnóstico de transtorno mental não recebiam tratamento.

Ele também cita estudos realizados em países de baixa e média renda nos quais a proporção de pessoas sem tratamento varia entre 60% e 80%. Em alguns contextos, pesquisas identificaram percentuais ainda maiores de pessoas sem diagnóstico e sem assistência.

O especialista destaca que a percepção de excesso de diagnósticos muitas vezes está associada à realidade das grandes cidades e à exposição do tema nas redes sociais.

Em outras regiões, especialmente no Norte e Nordeste do Brasil, a escassez de serviços especializados representa um problema muito mais evidente.

Para Polanczyk, embora possa haver excesso de diagnósticos em determinados grupos ou localidades, a principal preocupação em termos populacionais continua sendo a dificuldade de acesso à assistência.

Mais diagnósticos também significam mais acesso a benefícios

Outro fator apontado por Polanczyk é a importância que o diagnóstico passou a ter para garantir direitos e adaptações em diferentes ambientes.

Segundo ele, o reconhecimento formal de autismo ou TDAH pode facilitar o acesso a tratamentos, adaptações escolares, condições específicas para a realização de provas e ajustes no mercado de trabalho.

Isso contribuiu para aumentar a procura por avaliações. O problema, de acordo com o psiquiatra, é que muitas dessas adaptações podem ser necessárias mesmo quando a pessoa não preenche todos os critérios para um transtorno.

Entretanto, a organização dos sistemas educacional e judicial frequentemente condiciona o acesso a esses recursos à apresentação de um diagnóstico médico.

Polanczyk explica que essa exigência cria uma situação em que profissionais podem se sentir pressionados a estabelecer um diagnóstico para garantir que uma pessoa receba o suporte de que necessita.

Como consequência, os registros podem crescer sem que isso represente necessariamente um aumento equivalente da prevalência.

Para o especialista, trata-se de uma tensão ainda não resolvida: como garantir cuidados e adaptações para quem precisa sem transformar o diagnóstico psiquiátrico na única forma de acesso a esses recursos?

Quais são os riscos de um diagnóstico equivocado?

O aumento da conscientização sobre autismo e TDAH pode contribuir para a identificação de pessoas que precisam de acompanhamento. Mas os especialistas alertam que reconhecer sinais não é o mesmo que estabelecer um diagnóstico.

Kalil explica que a avaliação deve considerar critérios clínicos bem estabelecidos, a história do desenvolvimento e o impacto dos sintomas na vida da criança. Não basta identificar comportamentos isolados ou obter determinado resultado em um questionário de triagem.

Segundo o neurologista, diagnósticos inadequados podem provocar rotulação, ansiedade, intervenções desnecessárias e interpretações equivocadas sobre as dificuldades apresentadas.

Polanczyk acrescenta que, no caso do TDAH, um diagnóstico incorreto pode levar ao uso de medicamentos sem uma indicação clínica apropriada.

Embora os riscos dos estimulantes sejam considerados baixos quando existe indicação adequada, qualquer medicamento pode provocar efeitos indesejados. Para pessoas que não apresentam o transtorno, esses riscos podem não ser compensados por benefícios.

O psiquiatra também chama atenção para as consequências de intervenções psicoterapêuticas desnecessárias, que podem exigir tempo e recursos financeiros.

Na rede pública, a utilização de serviços especializados por pessoas que não precisam deles também pode reduzir a disponibilidade de atendimento para outros pacientes.

Há ainda possíveis impactos na maneira como crianças e adolescentes passam a compreender a própria identidade a partir de um diagnóstico equivocado.

“O objetivo não deve ser diagnosticar mais ou menos, mas suspeitar e diagnosticar melhor: reconhecer precocemente quem precisa de acompanhamento, sem transformar dificuldades normais do desenvolvimento em transtornos”, afirma Kalil.

Diagnóstico tardio também pode trazer consequências

Se o diagnóstico excessivo representa um risco, deixar de identificar pessoas que realmente apresentam autismo ou TDAH também pode provocar prejuízos importantes.

Segundo Kalil, o diagnóstico tardio pode prolongar dificuldades de aprendizagem, comunicação, comportamento, interação social e autoestima.

Em crianças e adolescentes, essas dificuldades podem aumentar o sofrimento emocional e comprometer a vida escolar e familiar.

Polanczyk destaca que existem evidências consolidadas sobre os benefícios de intervenções precoces, especialmente no autismo.

Isso ocorre porque determinadas fases do desenvolvimento cerebral apresentam maior plasticidade, favorecendo a resposta a estímulos ambientais e intervenções terapêuticas.

O psiquiatra explica que esse período pode ser especialmente importante para o desenvolvimento da linguagem e das habilidades sociais.

No caso do TDAH, a relação entre início precoce do tratamento e melhores resultados é mais complexa, porque os quadros identificados mais cedo frequentemente são também os mais graves.

Ainda assim, o especialista ressalta que a ausência de acompanhamento pode permitir o acúmulo de dificuldades ao longo da vida. Ele também menciona evidências de maior risco de depressão e suicídio entre pessoas que recebem diagnósticos tardios.

O vice-presidente da Associação Nacional para a Inclusão das Pessoas Autistas (Autistas Brasil) e pesquisador sobre desinformação sobre autismo na América Latina Arthur Ataide acrescenta que muitas pessoas chegam à vida adulta carregando uma história de incompreensão.

Foram crianças consideradas desatentas, indisciplinadas, estranhas, preguiçosas, desinteressadas ou pouco esforçadas. Algumas aprenderam, durante anos, que precisavam esconder determinadas características para conseguir participar dos espaços sociais”, afirma.

Isso pode contribuir para autoisolamento, dificuldade para construir e manter amizades, ausência ou redução importante de círculos de interação social, além de uma sensação persistente de não pertencimento.

“Há adultos que chegam aos serviços de saúde ou de educação relatando que passaram grande parte da vida sem compreender por que estabelecer relações, permanecer em determinados ambientes ou acompanhar as expectativas sociais parecia tão difícil”, destaca.

Essas consequências também podem aparecer na trajetória educacional e profissional. Crianças e adolescentes que não encontram formas adequadas de participação podem apresentar sofrimento escolar, afastamento, desengajamento e evasão.

Mais tarde, isso pode se expressar na dificuldade de ingressar e permanecer no ensino superior e no mercado de trabalho, segundo Ataide.

Por isso, os especialistas defendem que a identificação precoce seja acompanhada de avaliações cuidadosas e de intervenções adequadas às necessidades individuais.

Relatório propõe atendimento mesmo sem diagnóstico formal

Uma das principais recomendações da revisão é reorganizar os serviços para que o acesso ao apoio não dependa exclusivamente de um diagnóstico formal.

Na prática, isso permitiria que pessoas com dificuldades relacionadas à saúde mental, ao autismo ou ao TDAH recebessem apoio antes mesmo da conclusão de uma avaliação diagnóstica.

Para isso, os setores de saúde, educação e assistência social precisariam desenvolver maior flexibilidade e capacidade de identificar as necessidades de cada pessoa, sem deixar de reconhecer a importância das avaliações clínicas.

Miranda Wolpert, diretora de Saúde Mental da Wellcome, considera que a revisão representa uma contribuição importante para enfrentar o crescimento dos problemas de saúde mental.

Segundo ela, os avanços dependerão da ampliação de intervenções baseadas em evidências científicas, especialmente para as pessoas que mais precisam.

“Isso significará que as pessoas receberão ajuda mais cedo, reduzindo os impactos de longo prazo em sua educação, emprego e saúde”, afirma Wolpert.

Thea Stein, diretora executiva da Nuffield Trust Health, também avalia positivamente a proposta.

Para ela, os sistemas de atendimento passaram a exigir demais do diagnóstico e fizeram pouco para oferecer o apoio prático necessário às pessoas que enfrentam sofrimento psicológico.

A especialista ressalta, entretanto, que mudar os critérios de acesso não será suficiente se os serviços não tiverem condições de atender à demanda. A transição para um modelo baseado nas necessidades individuais só funcionará se o apoio estiver efetivamente disponível para quem precisa.

O que os números mostram sobre o autismo no Brasil?

Embora a revisão tenha analisado o cenário britânico, especialistas brasileiros destacam que a dificuldade de interpretar o crescimento dos diagnósticos também está presente no país.

Os dados nacionais ainda são escassos e recentes. O Censo de 2022 do Instituto Brasileiro de Geografia e Estatística (IBGE) apontou que aproximadamente 1,2% da população brasileira tinha diagnóstico de transtorno do espectro autista.

Kalil ressalta, entretanto, que esse percentual pode estar subestimado devido à existência de pessoas que ainda não receberam diagnóstico.

O especialista considera possível que a prevalência seja de aproximadamente 2% ou mais da população.

Nos Estados Unidos, Kalil cita dados dos Centros de Controle e Prevenção de Doenças (CDC) segundo os quais cerca de uma em cada 31 crianças de 8 anos foi identificada com autismo.

Os números reforçam a importância de distinguir a quantidade de pessoas diagnosticadas da prevalência real da condição.

No Brasil, Polanczyk destaca que regiões com maior acesso a avaliações médicas podem registrar mais diagnósticos sem que isso signifique, necessariamente, uma prevalência maior de autismo ou TDAH.

Inteligência artificial pode ajudar, mas não deve substituir atendimento humano

A revisão também analisa o potencial das tecnologias digitais e da inteligência artificial na assistência à saúde mental.

Embora reconheça que essas ferramentas podem contribuir para ampliar o acesso a determinados serviços, o relatório recomenda cautela em sua utilização.

Evidências mostram que intervenções digitais acompanhadas por profissionais apresentam resultados melhores do que aquelas utilizadas sem orientação.

As ferramentas não supervisionadas também enfrentam dificuldades para manter o envolvimento dos usuários durante períodos prolongados.

O relatório observa que algumas terapias digitais regulamentadas já receberam recomendações condicionais do Instituto Nacional de Excelência em Saúde e Cuidados do Reino Unido (NICE).

Entretanto, as recomendações relacionadas às tecnologias digitais ainda são classificadas como sustentadas por evidências moderadas ou emergentes.

A revisão defende que ferramentas que prometem benefícios clínicos sejam avaliadas de acordo com padrões apropriados para intervenções de saúde. Também estabelece uma ressalva importante: a inteligência artificial nunca deve ser a única resposta oferecida a uma pessoa em situação de risco.

Um dos exemplos analisados envolve um sistema digital de triagem que apresentou bom desempenho técnico, mas benefício limitado para a organização do atendimento.

Isso ocorreu porque os critérios utilizados para identificar pacientes prioritários eram excessivamente restritos e concentrados em situações de crise.

Como consequência, muitas pessoas com comprometimentos significativos acabavam encaminhadas para a mesma fila de espera, sem uma diferenciação adequada de suas necessidades.

O exemplo demonstra que a eficiência técnica de uma ferramenta não garante, por si só, melhorias na assistência.

Pesquisadores alertam também que modelos de inteligência artificial treinados com dados clínicos históricos podem reproduzir desigualdades já existentes nos serviços de saúde.

Mudança no atendimento depende de mais profissionais e recursos

Embora a revisão proponha uma transformação na forma como os serviços identificam e atendem pessoas com problemas de saúde mental, os especialistas ressaltam que as recomendações dependem da capacidade de implementação.

A ampliação dos serviços, a disponibilidade de profissionais qualificados e a oferta efetiva de apoio são condições necessárias para que a mudança produza resultados.

Para os pesquisadores, a principal contribuição do relatório é deslocar o foco do debate: mais importante do que discutir exclusivamente se existem diagnósticos excessivos é identificar se as pessoas que realmente precisam de ajuda estão sendo reconhecidas e recebendo atendimento em tempo adequado.

articles.title: Pope's health should not be taken 'for granted', says top Vatican diplomat
articles.summary: Archbishop Paul Gallagher tells the BBC there was no sign of the Pope's ill health prior to his operation this week.
articles.body:
Pope Leo XIV's health should not be taken "for granted", a British senior Vatican official told the BBC.

Archbishop Paul Gallagher, the Vatican's foreign minister since 2014, said the news of the Pope's ill health was "a bit of a game changer", adding "it's going to make things a bit different".

The Pope was diagnosed with lung adenocarcinoma following surgery to remove a lower lobe of his right lung.

Speaking on Tuesday after the Pope's operation was announced, but before his cancer diagnosis, Archbishop Gallagher said: "I think we were maybe taking him a little bit for granted."

The 71-year-old had surgery at Rome's Gemelli Hospital on Tuesday afternoon, which the Vatican said had been "successful" and proceeded without complications.

Speaking to Radio 4's the Sunday Programme, due to air this weekend, the Archbishop said: "It's in some ways I think going to be a bit of a game changer after having the latter years of Pope Francis when he was in the wheelchair.

"And Pope Leo comes along and he's sporty and he seems to be in excellent health, and now we're told that he's not in excellent health and things have got to be sorted out."

Asked how it will make things different going forward, the Archbishop said church figures might have assumed "that he was not quite like the rest of us who are very aware of our vulnerabilities and the ageing process".

He went on: "But lots of us have been through similar experiences at different times in our lives, and we've got through them, and so we hope it's going to be the same case with Pope Leo.

"I am concerned. I think we've got to ask the question: how was it discovered? What happened?"

The Vatican has said the Pope is showing steady improvement in hospital, and he was expected to lead Sunday prayers.

They had stressed that the Pope had shown no symptoms of infection or illness prior to the procedure.

The Angelus prayer is traditionally recited at the Vatican, overlooking crowds in St Peter's Square but has sometimes been given from a hospital window by previous popes when necessary.

No date has been given for Pope Leo's hospital discharge, but recovery was expected to take around a week.

Leo himself announced the news of his operation during his weekly Sunday prayers, telling the crowd in St Peter's Square that doctors had found a nodule on his lung.

Nodules are quite common and not necessarily cancerous, but after it was examined the medical team confirmed it was, "as suspected by pre-operative tests", the Vatican said.

Archbishop Gallagher, who is from Liverpool, also said he expected the Pope to visit the UK at some point.

"We have exchanged a little bit," he said. "He's just beginning to think about what he might do in 2027, but it's still very much at the examining the possibilities (stage)".

He would "bring a spirit of renewed hope", said the Archbishop, after the Pope received a rapturous welcome in France and Spain earlier this year.

"But these things do take quite a lot of planning, and so you don't just do it overnight."

articles.title: Fernando Cerveró, médico: "El alivio del dolor es, probablemente, una actividad inevitable para los sanitarios"
articles.standfirst: El dolor puede cambiar la forma en la que nos sentimos, somos y vivimos
articles.summary: El dolor puede cambiar la forma en la que nos sentimos, somos y vivimos
articles.body: Uno de los aspectos que más condiciona la vida de muchas personas es el dolor. Atravesar una etapa en la que esta es la tónica en tu vida y en tu forma de vivir puede ser un auténtico suplicio. Es por esto que se homenajea a esta tan terrible situación en el día de hoy. Tal y como se desvela en el blog de la Sociedad Española contra el Dolor, el doctor español Fernando Cerveró; "el alivio del dolor a través del estudio y del desarrollo de nuevas y mejores terapias es, probablemente, la actividad más ineludible que debemos realidar", refiriéndose a los médicos y personal sanitario. Desde la asociación citada con anterioridad, mencionan que los objetivos de su iniciativa son varios y múltiples. Uno de ellos es aumentar la concienciación, educando sobre la magnitud y el impacto de las condiciones de dolor concretas y específicas y que, en muchas ocasiones, son subestimadas o mal gestionadas. Además, consideran que una de las fórmulas para atajar el tratamiento del dolor es fomentar la investigación impulsándola con una mayor financiación y colaboración. Por otro lado, debemos mejorar la educación, proporcionando una mayor y mejor calidad de recursos educativos. Este año se conmemora un dolor muy concreto y se pone el foco en él. Este es el dolor neuropático, que es un tipo de dolor crónico que aparece por una lesión o por un mal funcionamiento del sistema nervioso, ya sea tanto en los nervios periféricos, como en la médula espinal o el cerebro; pero no por un daño en los músculos o las articulaciones. Normalmente, este tipo de dolor causa una sensación de ardor o quemazón que se mantiene constante y que se siente caliente e incluso abrasador. Muchas personas mencionan que sufren una sensación similar a las descargas eléctricas o a los pinchazos, que son repentinos, punzantes o breves. En ocasiones, también se puede desarrollar la llamada alodinia que es un dolor causado por un estímulo que normalmente no duele pero que, con el simple roce de la ropa o de las sábanas molesta y duele. También se puede dar la hiperalgesia, que es una respuesta al dolor mucho más intensa de lo normal o, incluso, hormigueos y entumecimiento, llegando a tener sensación de que te clavan agujas o de que tienes pérdida parcial de la sensibilidad o hipoestesia. Concienciar sobre el dolor es necesario para ser más empáticos y remar en el camino de la ayuda a quienes se ven obligados a convivir con él.

articles.title: As Israel blocks PA funding, the West Bank’s healthcare system is failing
articles.summary: Hospitals across the occupied West Bank have been hit by a funding shortage.
articles.body:
Beit Jala, occupied West Bank – Khaldoun Atwan starts each day in the oncology ward at Beit Jala Government Hospital, not knowing what barriers will come his way.

The Nabi Yunis checkpoint in Halhul seems to be “always closed”, so the head of the daytime oncology unit at the hospital leaves his car and finishes the commute from Hebron by taxi.

“More than once, by God, I found the mirror broken. I found the wiper broken,” he said about his journey through an area where settlers are now active.

Traversing a dizzying array of gates and checkpoints opening or closing at will, he does not know whether he will reach the hospital, whether his patients will, or whether the drugs they need will be on the shelf when they do.

Beit Jala is the only government hospital in Bethlehem governorate, home to some 320,000 people. Inside his tiny, spartan office, Atwan is struggling to keep up with his cancer patients who have regressed because they missed crucial appointments or essential drugs needed for their chemotherapy treatment.

Not even during the second Intifada, he recalls, was drug supply an issue. Now, it’s inescapable.

“Everything’s short … whatever’s available we give,” he said. “It’s a disaster.”

The Palestinian Authority (PA)’s finances have collapsed over the last three years due to a reduction in international aid and disruptions in Israel’s transfers of tax receipts. Israel’s actions in the occupied West Bank since October 2023, including widespread road closures, checkpoints and a series of settler pogroms against Palestinian communities, have also impacted the economy.

As a result, the occupied West Bank’s healthcare system is rapidly deteriorating, with staff receiving just half their salaries, while the PA can’t pay for essential medications.

Alongside others nervously pacing in the courtyard, an older cancer patient from a village in Bethlehem governorate stood at the entrance of the hospital, weighing with his son what to do. “Every month they do their best, the doctors and the cleaning staff, but they aren’t provided with anything,” he said.

Ministry clinics are now operating part-time, with doctors seeing well more than 100 patients a day when they are. Now, even a doctor’s visit is rushed and unaffordable: “If we want to go to the doctor for a checkup, we need 200 shekels [$65],” said an older cancer patient.

“It’s not a story of there being no staff,” said Iyad Dari, the attending physician at the dialysis unit at Beit Jala. Getting paid only half their salaries, “the government employee is working just two or three days a week, because he hasn’t got enough to come in for his full hours,” he added. As a result, the hospital ends up covering emergency cases only.

“At first, [patients] were [angry]. But now everyone understands: Everyone’s suffering,” Dari said.

The medical supplies crisis in Beit Jala and across the West Bank is the result of Israel’s withholding of tax revenues earmarked for the PA, an action spearheaded by Israeli Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich.

“This crisis is very predictable, and we saw it coming 100 percent,” said Milena Ansari of Physicians for Human Rights Israel. Even before the genocidal war on Gaza began in October 2023, Israel was periodically withholding tax revenues, endangering the Ministry of Health’s coffers, Milena said.

According to Yosef Ojra, an internal medicine specialist at Beit Jala, the withheld revenues have depleted the Health Ministry’s funds to pay medical suppliers, who are now withholding their services. The ongoing borrowing of supplies between the public and private arms of healthcare has greatly strained private clinics, pharmacies and hospitals.

Hisham Amle, an oncologist at the hospital, said shortages are “an old problem, not a new one”, but that about 90 percent of important items – for chemotherapy, above all – used to be there. Now, even immunotherapies and biologics are missing, and cancer treatment runs on an unbroken chain. “If the patient misses a session or two, he’s lost all the treatment before it,” he said.

“When I first took over the department, the drugs were available,” said Atwan, the lead oncology nurse. He then began to list all the crucial drugs he was now missing for his patients. “There’s not one single complete protocol I’ve got.”

Khuloud Dweib, the hospital’s director of pharmacy, said the ministry recently managed to obtain eight previously missing oncology drugs and four biologics. This should be enough for between a month and a half and two months. But many other drugs are still out of stock, she said.

Unlike in Gaza, Israel is not blocking medicines from entering the West Bank, Ansari noted. The problem is “strictly” that the PA has no money to buy them. But “Israel has the primary legal obligation as an occupying power,” she notes, to ensure adequate medical care and access to occupied populations.

For all of the southern West Bank, Beit Jala’s hospital is the only public option available for cancer and dialysis treatment, with patients coming from Bethlehem and Hebron governorates, parts of occupied East Jerusalem and sometimes Jericho.

But as Israeli checkpoints and gates multiply, reaching the hospital has become a nightmare. Dari described a dialysis patient from Nahalin, with an appointment at seven or eight in the morning, whose village was sealed. “He sat about four, five hours at the checkpoint,” Dari said. Then he took the long way round, through Jaba, Surif, Halhul and Hebron, and reached the unit at four in the afternoon. A normal journey costs about 10 shekels. “A detour like this costs more than 100 shekels,” Dari said, and some patients need dialysis four times a week.

The ministry’s central supply warehouse, meanwhile, is in Nablus, Dweib said – and an hour-and-a-half drive can now take six to 10 hours when closures hit.

Often, Atwan’s patients require treatments split between his unit and the Augusta Victoria Hospital in occupied East Jerusalem. Before the war, cancer patients from the West Bank routinely received medical permits to enter Jerusalem. Some treatments are in Beit Jala, while others are only available in East Jerusalem. But there are no guarantees any more that patients can reach Jerusalem. “I’ve got a cancer patient … He waited on a referral, and there’s no treatment, and after all the running around it comes back he’s security-rejected, too,” Atwan said. “I mean, he doesn’t get a permit to go to [Augusta Victoria]? Where’s he supposed to go?”

Atwan recalled patients who became neutropenic due to missed treatment sessions, and one was lucky not to end up with sepsis. “These are disasters.”

He’s not sure exactly how many cancer patients he’s lost due to missed and incomplete treatments; many of the poorer patients, he said, simply go home and die there.

‘I’ve started cutting back, not taking much’

As crowds swell at front desks and people wait at the hospital’s entrance, a nervous exhaustion percolates through the hospital’s aged halls. “People are really tense. Everyone’s scared,” Dari said.

Atwan, who receives half his salary, struggles to cover his commute from Hebron and help support his daughters at university.

“Let’s not talk about our state of mind – we’ll start crying, for God’s sake,” said Atwan. “Our morale is at rock bottom … We smile in spite of ourselves.”

Amid mass unemployment with labour permits systematically revoked, more sick Palestinians are pushed towards public hospitals just as those hospitals have less to give. Hospitals “will prioritise someone who will actually pay them”, Ansari added.

Ahmed, a Palestinian from Bethlehem with a medical degree, would check every couple of days with the pharmacist to see if they had Humira, an injection every two weeks that his sister with Crohn’s disease needs. For three months, the pharmacists were out of stock. Buying directly from the pharmaceutical company would cost about 2,000 shekels ($650) for one or two injections. “We couldn’t afford that,” he said. “So we just struggled until it became available again.”

The elderly cancer patient from a village facing settler pogroms has cut back on his own medication. “It’s not supplied regularly,” he said. A course of it costs 20,000 shekels ($6,500). “I’ve started cutting back, not taking much,” he added.

Amid supply and staffing shortages, surgery backlogs have piled up. Sayed Ayyad, 22, from al-Eizariya, fell during an accident, fracturing his ankle badly last month. With serious operations taking priority, he waited three weeks for a slot.

“They told me there’s 60 people waiting for an operation,” he said. “One day we couldn’t do the surgery because there were no medicines, no painkillers, no anaesthetic, nothing.”

Khuloud Dweib, who heads the pharmacy department at Beit Jala, has to manage the worsening crisis as patients struggle with their health and finances. “There’s no security. We don’t have political, or health, or even financial security,” she said.

She’s left thinking of cases like a young man with multiple sclerosis studying medicine in Egypt. The Health Ministry used to provide his medicine through private purchase until the company stopped supplying without payment. His mother came to see her. “I want to sell my house so I can get the injection for my son,” the mother told her. “Because he’s in Egypt, away from home, studying, and … he’s stopped seeing, stopped walking.”

“So, what can I tell you,” Dweib said, fighting back the tears. “God help people.”

The medical staff fear that with their supplies being hollowed out, they could face a similar fate to their colleagues in Gaza who have been kidnapped or killed.

“We know that at any moment we could be targeted as medical staff, just because we’re medical personnel providing services to people,” Dweib said. “We’re a father and a mother in this society.”

Nobody in the ageing hospital wards sees an end in sight. “The longer we stay, the worse the situation gets,” said Dari.

At three o’clock each afternoon, Atwan has to leave in the hope that he can reach Bab az-Zawiya in Hebron, where he waits for a shared taxi.

“Maybe there’ll be a checkpoint for me, maybe there won’t be,” he said. It’s not so different from the conundrums his patients face. “When a patient gets sick, it’s his luck if the medicine’s there,” he said. “We’ve got no future. I swear: We’ve got no future.”

articles.title: Bournemouth recovery driver sentenced after runaway car crush
articles.summary: CCTV footage captured the vehicle rolling down the road, dragging driver Sean Baker along.
articles.body:
A vehicle recovery driver has been sentenced after he failed to secure a Range Rover that later rolled down a hill, dragging him along and crushing a member of the public who tried to help.

Sean Baker, a driver for GRS Recovery Bournemouth, was sentenced to 14 weeks in prison, suspended for one year, at Bournemouth Crown Court on Friday.

CCTV showed the two-tonne vehicle rolling down Exeter Crescent during a recovery operation on 22 March 2024, with Baker caught by a rear wheel.

Kai Dransfield was on a break from his job at TGI Fridays when he saw Baker trapped under the runaway car "hanging on for dear life" and tried to help, only to be struck by the 4x4.

Dransfield said: "He made eye contact with me, and my first thought was to just grab him to try and help him."

But in his attempt to help, Dransfield was hit by the vehicle and pulled underneath it.

The vehicle rolled over both of his legs, causing serious injuries including multiple broken bones in his legs and fractures to his spine, according to the Health and Safety Executive (HSE).

Dransfield continues to suffer chronic pain more than two years after the incident, and has difficulty walking.

An HSE investigation found Baker had initially attached a winch to the front of the Range Rover, which would have prevented the vehicle rolling away if the handbrake was released or failed.

But Baker later removed the winch, jacked up the vehicle and placed skates beneath the rear wheels, it said.

Because the wheels were not secured with chocks, and no breakaway cables were attached, there was nothing preventing the vehicle from rolling backwards when it was lowered on to the skates.

The investigation concluded Baker failed to take reasonable care for his own safety and that of others by not following established recovery procedures.

The HSE also found his actions fell below the standard expected of a competent and experienced recovery driver.

Baker later pleaded guilty to breaching Section 7 of the Health and Safety at Work etc. Act 1974.

Speaking after the sentencing hearing, HSE inspector Alexander Ashen said: "Sean Baker was an experienced recovery driver.

"Failing to properly secure a vehicle weighing more than two tonnes on a steep hill was a fundamental error.

"This happened in a busy town centre, close to restaurants and car parks, with vehicles, motorcyclists and pedestrians regularly passing through the area.

"Sean Baker's failings were substantial, they exposed everyone nearby to risk and resulted in a member of the public, who stepped in to help, suffering life-changing injuries."

articles.title: Pope discharged from hospital days after lung cancer surgery
articles.summary: The pontiff will give the traditional Angelus prayer and blessing in St Peter's Square on Sunday.
articles.body:
Pope Leo XIV has been discharged from Rome's Gemelli Hospital, just four days after an operation to remove a cancerous growth from his lung.

The 71-year-old walked unaided to his waiting car, stopping to speak to well-wishers.

The Vatican said the Pope will give the traditional Angelus prayer and blessing to a crowd in St Peter's Square on Sunday, as he did last week when he surprised the world by announcing the surgery.

On Friday, photographs were released of the Pope celebrating Mass and distributing communion in hospital for staff.

A statement from his doctors said blood tests and a chest X-ray showed "steady improvement" following his operation.

The surgery on Tuesday, which lasted for 90 minutes, included the removal of the lower lobe of the Pope's right lung. The results of further tests to check for any sign that the cancer has spread have not yet been announced.

The Pope also spoke to Russian President Vladimir Putin on Friday, in their first call since June 2025. The Vatican said the call was to urge "dialogue and peace".

It came as Russia's bombardment of cities across Ukraine intensifies, with a growing number of civilian casualties and no sign of Putin being ready to halt the invasion.

The Pope also called for a humanitarian ceasefire in the Ukrainian city of Oleshkiy, occupied by Russia and under constant shelling, to allow people to be evacuated and for the urgent delivery of food and medicine. The BBC recently reported on residents there being forced to eat garden weeds to survive.

The Pope's schedule has been cleared completely until 20 October, so his reappearance in public so soon is a surprise and will be some relief for Catholics around the world.

Those close to the Pope said he was keen not to delay a trip to Latin America, planned for early November and which includes a visit to Peru, where he was a missionary for many years.

It is not yet clear whether he might be fit to travel or require further treatment.

articles.title: Leonardo DiCaprio's 'dad bod' puts spotlight on dangerous belly fat — and how to lose it
articles.summary: Leonardo DiCaprio's beach photos sparked a 'dad bod' debate, as a trainer warns that excess belly fat and visceral fat carry serious health risks.
articles.body: Recent beach photos of actor Leonardo DiCaprio have reignited the "dad bod" debate — and raised questions about whether carrying a little extra weight around the middle can pose hidden health risks. The popular term generally describes a softer physique with extra weight around the midsection. While appearance alone isn’t an indicator of health, excess abdominal fat — particularly visceral fat surrounding the organs — has been linked to an increased risk of heart disease, diabetes and other medical conditions, according to Cleveland Clinic. YOUR WAISTLINE COULD REVEAL A HIDDEN HEART RISK YOUR BMI MISSES, MAJOR STUDY FINDS Marfred Suazo, a New York City-based personal trainer known as Fonz the Trainer, spoke with Fox News Digital about the potential risks associated with excess abdominal fat and ways to reduce it. Suazo, who has not trained DiCaprio, defines a dad bod as a "loss of structure," an increase in waist circumference and a loss of muscle mass. "Maybe you're losing structure in your day-to-day eating … moving a lot less, taking fewer steps per day," he said of potential causes. "And typically you're eating and drinking more than you're moving. And the body just starts showcasing that stuff." BEST FOODS FOR REDUCING DANGEROUS BELLY FAT AND PROTECTING HEART HEALTH An expanding waistline can be an important indicator of health risk. According to the National Institute of Diabetes and Digestive and Kidney Diseases, men with a waist circumference greater than 40 inches have a higher risk of developing health problems, including type 2 diabetes and heart disease. Visceral fat — which lies deep within the abdomen and surrounds internal organs — has also been linked to a higher risk of cardiovascular disease, Cleveland Clinic states. "We want to try to mitigate these things as best as possible before they become an issue," Suazo said. Getting rid of a dad bod Reversing a "dad bod" starts with getting nutrition in check, according to Suazo. That includes understanding daily calorie intake and getting an appropriate balance of protein, carbohydrates and fats. Also among his favorite exercises are pull-ups. articles.title: A courageous teenager battling brain cancer gets the surprise of a lifetime from his beloved Florida Gators
articles.summary: It started with just the kind of news that is every parent’s worst nightmare.
articles.body: It started with just the kind of news that is every parent’s worst nightmare. Like so many other teenagers, Jonah Blick was enjoying what should have been a fun-filled day out with friends at the lake. What followed on that ill-fated hot summer’s day in August would change the 14-year-old’s life forever. The seemingly perfectly healthy and always active youngster from Georgia suffered a massive seizure, with scans later revealing three brain tumors. “We don’t have any health issues in our family. Literally was at a checkup eight weeks ago, all good. I don’t know why, we thought it would never be us,” Randi Blick, Jonah’s mother, told CNN Sports. “I, genuinely in a million years, never would have thought it would happen to our son,” she added. A week after that trip to the lake came news the Blick family had been dreading: Jonah was battling a rare and aggressive form of pediatric brain cancer. It was a devastating setback for the family, but the courageous teen has already successfully undergone two major surgeries in Boston and Atlanta and is currently having radiation treatment. “It’s incredible. He’s the bravest kid I’ve ever met. He’s handled it with poise and understanding but still, he charges forward at it and he’s ready to go,” said Adam Blick, Jonah’s father. Jonah himself is remaining positive while keeping his spirits up thanks to the love, support and encouragement of his family, friends and all those doctors and nurses who care so much for him. The teenager is not just courageous – he’s also very passionate about sports. He enjoys soccer and basketball and when it comes to college football, there’s only one team for Jonah – his beloved Florida Gators. So just imagine his joy and elation when those nearest and dearest to him recently gathered to give him an epic send-off to the Sunshine State to see his favorite team in action at the University of Florida in Gainesville. It was the surprise of a lifetime, and one made possible by the Atlanta-based nonprofit YES DAY. “Our whole North Star, our whole guiding principle, is that we can’t always control what happens to someone. We can’t fix your diagnosis, but we can absolutely bring you joy into the middle of hard things,” says YES DAY founder Jodi Sonenshine. Before leaving for Gainesville, Jonah told CNN Sports he had no idea his dream surprise was happening. Instead, he thought he was off to another medical appointment. “It was crazy, it was very unexpected,” Jonah said. “Watching all the games, (it’s) a very cool atmosphere. The atmosphere, it’s crazy,” he added while reflecting on what makes it so special to be a fan of the Florida Gators. The trip itself was everything Jonah could have possibly dreamed of. Upon arrival at Ben Hill Griffin Stadium in Gainesville, the star-struck teen was given a chance to tour the Gators’ locker room and meet the team including his favorite player, Florida quarterback Aaron Philo. Then came some VIP seats in a suite to witness the Gators’ victory against the Florida Atlantic University Owls. “You know, he’s always the kindest kid in the class. The story about him was, you know, the first high school party he went to and a couple of (his) friends weren’t invited. He said, ‘I’m going to remind whoever that these people need to be invited because they’re not as outgoing or whatever.’ That’s his personality,” Adam Blick said. “And for that to be repaid to him, in this type of kindness coming out, I mean, he’s kind and he’s brave. I can’t believe, it seems like only a few years ago he was afraid to be in the basement by himself and look at him now. It’s crazy,” he added. “It’s been a lot, but we’re learning a lot, and he’s so strong, and, you know, not many people can say they birthed their own hero,” Randi Blick said. “But we’re now part of a club we never wanted to be in.” According to the American Cancer Society, just under 5,000 children and teenagers are diagnosed with a brain tumor each year in the United States. The Blick family say they’ve been strengthened and encouraged by an amazing show of support and love from a truly caring community, and they now want to share an important message when it comes to helping other parents who may be facing their own heartache over a child’s diagnosis. “Jonah had his first seizure on August 8. From that, to go through two surgeries, to learning more about cancer than I ever wanted to know, we couldn’t do it without the people that were here today,” Adam said. “Really find your community, find your support, find your people that are like this. The people at Children’s Healthcare of Atlanta are amazing. The people at Boston’s Children Hospital are unbelievable. I mean, they’re the smartest people you’ll know, and the kindest people you know, and they’re all doing this out of the kindness of their heart,” he added. Jonah is now continuing his radiation course before his medical team decides on his next stage of treatment. For now, though, it’s one never-to-be-forgotten weekend in Florida that’s offered a moment of respite alongside his family and friends. Simply put, the people who mean the most to him in life. “They’re very nice. They care a lot about me and they’re checking up on me all the time,” Jonah said. “Just stay with your family, stay with your friends,” he said. And as Sonenshine put it on the family’s online support page: “For now, we keep taking it one day at a time, finding the joy wherever we can and surrounding this family with as much love as humanly possible.” If you want to help and support Jonah and his family, just head to the Ian’s Friends foundation, which funds research for pediatric brain tumors, and you can keep up to date with Jonah’s progress here.

articles.title: Hackers hide dangerous fake AI downloads behind Google ads
articles.summary: A fake Claude AI download scam uses Google ads and Bing redirects to trick Mac users into pasting a hidden malicious command in their Terminal.
articles.body: You search Google for Claude, the popular AI assistant, and spot a sponsored result. The link points to Bing, Microsoft's search engine. Nothing immediately screams scam. However, that click could send you through several websites before landing on a convincing fake Claude download page designed to trick you into running a dangerous command on your Mac. Security researchers at Push Security uncovered a clever attack that uses legitimate search engine links to hide a malicious installer. The technique, which researchers jokingly call "Adception," takes advantage of how Google ads and Bing redirects work. Even more concerning, the fake installer shows one command on the screen while secretly copying another. Here's how the scam works and what you should know before downloading AI software. Join our upcoming CyberGuy LIVE class: 5 Ways to Travel Smarter and Save Money In this free live online class, Kurt "CyberGuy" Knutsson will share five practical ways to protect your trip and your wallet this holiday travel season. You’ll learn how to secure your phone and personal information, find better travel deals, avoid common scams, save money on bookings and use technology to make your travels easier and less stressful. No technical experience is needed. Join us Saturday, October 31, at 11 AM ET / 8 AM PT. Register free now at CyberGuyLive.com. HACKERS HIJACK VERIFIED STREAMING ACCOUNT TO SPREAD MALWARE, RESEARCHERS FIND How a fake AI download scam starts with Google The attack begins with a Google search for "Claude Mac." According to Push Security, researchers discovered a sponsored search result that displayed bing.com as its destination. That address might seem reassuring because Bing belongs to Microsoft. However, clicking the advertisement sends users through a series of redirects. First, Google's advertising system processes the click. Next, Bing's legitimate click-tracking service forwards the browser to a compromised WordPress website belonging to a South American retailer. Finally, that website sends the visitor to a fake Claude download page. The final website, claude-desk-code[.]com, imitates the real Claude download experience. It presents what appears to be a legitimate macOS installation option. By the time someone reaches the page, they may have little reason to suspect the journey began with a malicious advertisement. Researchers say the attackers deliberately used a real Bing search result for a compromised website. This allowed the attackers to display Bing's legitimate domain in the Google advertisement while using Bing's click-tracking redirect to send visitors toward the malicious destination. Why the fake Claude installer is difficult to spot The scammers added another layer of deception to make their operation harder to detect. The compromised retailer's website checks whether visitors arrived through Bing and whether their browsers send certain information. Meanwhile, the fake Claude website checks whether visitors came from Google or Bing. Someone who visits the malicious website directly may see a 404 error page instead of the fake installer. That behavior can make it harder for security scanners to investigate the attack because they may never encounter the page that victims actually see. Push Security calls this technique cloaking. Attackers use it to control who reaches their malicious content while showing something harmless to other visitors. In this case, the researchers observed two separate checks designed to protect the attack from unwanted attention. The result is a carefully constructed path that makes a dangerous destination appear more trustworthy than it really is. The fake Claude download button hides a dangerous command Here's where the attack gets particularly sneaky. The fake Claude page displays an installation command that appears to come directly from Anthropic, the company behind Claude. The command references Claude's legitimate website and looks like something a technically confident Mac user might recognize. However, the page's Copy button places a completely different command on the clipboard. According to Push Security, the substituted command uses Base64 encoding to conceal an attacker-controlled website. When someone runs the pasted command in Mac Terminal, it first displays a reassuring message claiming that Claude is being downloaded from its official website. Behind the scenes, the command decodes the hidden address, downloads a remote script and sends it directly to the Mac's Z shell for execution. That means the person running the command sees references to Claude's legitimate website even though the Mac is executing code from an unrelated server. This attack follows a technique known as InstallFix, a variation of ClickFix. These scams convince people to execute malicious commands themselves, often by disguising the instructions as a software installation or troubleshooting step. Push Security identified several additional websites associated with the same malicious toolkit, which it tracks internally as AcSig. The researchers found matching installation commands and similar fake installer interfaces across those sites. What happens if someone runs the fake Claude installer? The research confirms that the malicious command is designed to download a remote script from an attacker-controlled server and pass it directly to the Mac's Z shell for execution. However, Push Security's published findings do not identify the final payload or establish what the downloaded script does after execution. That uncertainty is important. Running an untrusted Terminal command can give malicious code an opportunity to operate with the permissions of the person executing it. Depending on the script, an attacker could potentially steal information, modify files or install additional software. The researchers have not confirmed those specific outcomes in this campaign. The bigger concern is how easily the attack can persuade someone to bypass their own caution. The user voluntarily pastes the command, believing it came from a legitimate software provider. Meanwhile, the actual destination stays hidden inside encoded text. Push Security reports that four out of five ClickFix attacks it detects reach victims through search engines. That figure comes from the company's own detection data rather than a measurement of all attacks worldwide. Still, it shows why malicious search advertisements deserve attention. Google suspends accounts behind malicious ads Google confirms it has taken action against the advertiser accounts associated with the reported campaign. "We've suspended the advertiser accounts running the reported campaign. Using ads to distribute malware is an egregious violation of our policies, and we consistently update our detection systems to stay ahead of bad actors' evolving tactics," a Google spokesperson told CyberGuy. Google also says attackers use cloaking to show its advertising review systems different content from what people actually see. The company says it continues monitoring attempts to evade its protections and updating its detection systems. Microsoft responds to malicious AI download campaign Microsoft also responded to CyberGuy's request for comment, confirming that its security protections identify the malicious indicators described in the research. A Microsoft spokesperson told CyberGuy, "We take reports of malicious online activity seriously and continuously work to help protect customers from evolving threats. Microsoft Defender protections detect and block the malicious indicators identified in the report." We also reached out to Anthropic for comment on the findings but did not hear back before our deadline. ANTI-SCAM SETTINGS ON IPHONE, PIXEL AND GALAXY YOU SHOULD CHECK How to protect your Mac from fake AI downloads You don't need to understand every line of computer code to avoid this scam. A few precautions can help you recognize suspicious downloads before they put your Mac at risk. 1. Download Claude directly from Anthropic Instead of searching for a download and clicking the first sponsored result, go directly to Claude's official download page. Anthropic provides a macOS download there, so you can install the desktop application without relying on an unfamiliar website. You can also access Claude through your browser at claude.ai. 2. Treat unexpected Terminal instructions as a warning Be especially careful when a website tells you to copy a command into your Mac's Terminal. Terminal commands can download software, change system settings and execute scripts. Even legitimate-looking instructions can become dangerous when they come from an untrusted source. For the regular Claude desktop app, Anthropic provides a downloadable installer. You don't need to paste a command from a search advertisement to get started. 3. Check what a website actually copies A website's Copy button can place different text on your clipboard than what appears on the page. Before running an unfamiliar command, paste it into a plain-text editor and compare it with the instructions. Watch for unexplained web addresses, encoded strings or commands that download and immediately execute remote scripts. However, even a command that looks harmless may contain hidden risks. When in doubt, stop and verify the instructions with the software developer. 4. Keep your Mac updated and use strong antivirus protection Install macOS security updates and keep your browser current. Additionally, use strong antivirus software that offers real-time protection against malicious downloads and suspicious activity. Security software may help detect harmful scripts or their effects, although no antivirus product can guarantee protection against every attack. Get my picks for the best 2026 antivirus protection winners for your Windows, Mac, Android & iOS devices at Cyberguy.com 5. Be skeptical of sponsored search results A sponsored placement means someone paid to promote a link. It does not guarantee that the destination is safe. Before clicking, check the advertiser by selecting the three dots next to a Google search ad. You can review who paid for it and check the advertiser's verification status. Google's Ads Transparency Center at adstransparency.google.com/ offers another way to research advertisers. Always confirm you're visiting the software developer's official website before downloading anything. If an ad looks suspicious, use its three-dot menu to select "Report this ad." What to do if you already ran the fake Claude command If you pasted an installation command from a suspicious Claude website into Terminal and pressed Return, treat your Mac as potentially compromised. The researchers have not established what the final payload does, so don't assume everything is safe simply because nothing unusual appears on your screen. WHY VERIFIED SOCIAL MEDIA ACCOUNTS CAN STILL LEAD YOU INTO A SCAM Kurt's key takeaways What concerns me most about this attack is how much effort the scammers put into making everything look familiar. You start with Google, pass through a legitimate Microsoft service and eventually arrive at a page that looks like it belongs to a popular AI company. Then, with one click of a Copy button, the website quietly substitutes a command that could put your Mac at risk. I've always encouraged people to pay attention to website addresses before downloading software. That's still important, but this case shows why checking the address alone may not be enough. The attackers used trusted services to disguise where their link was taking people. My advice is to go straight to the software developer's official website, especially when installing AI tools. And whenever a download page asks you to run something in Terminal, make sure you understand exactly what you're authorizing. A few extra seconds of caution could save you from a much bigger headache. Would you trust a software download if it appeared in a Google ad and showed a familiar Microsoft link, or has this kind of scam made you question whether search results can be trusted at all? articles.title: Younger men are attracted to older women for reasons that have nothing to do with looks
articles.summary: Tammy Nelson says older women dating younger men are redefining desire and aging, as new research suggests traditional age-gap rules are loosening.
articles.body: Relationships between older women and younger men are drawing more attention as traditional dating expectations continue to shift. Tammy Nelson, a board-certified sexologist, sex therapist and integrative relationship therapist in Los Angeles, told Fox News Digital that she is seeing greater interest in these age-gap relationships. "Older women and younger men are now a thing," she said. "I know a lot of older women, even my age, that are dating or … being attracted to younger men." What the research shows Polling and research in recent years suggests that traditional dating rules around age may be loosening. POLITICAL FIGHTS CAN RIP COUPLES APART — THERAPIST SHARES 3 WAYS TO SAVE A RELATIONSHIP A 2023 Bumble poll of 26,849 dating-app users across more than 20 countries found that 59% of women were more open to dating someone younger, while 35% said they had become less judgmental about age-gap relationships. A 2025 study published in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences similarly found that men and women were both slightly more attracted to younger partners after blind dates. The study, which included adults ages 22 to 85, measured initial attraction rather than long-term relationship outcomes. "This preference for youth among women will be shocking to many people," Paul Eastwick, a psychology professor at the University of California, Davis, and lead author of the study, said in a university news release. "But women’s preferences on the dates themselves revealed something else entirely." "You can teach each other and share with each other a different perspective about the world." A separate 2024 analysis of nearly 36,000 couples across 29 European countries found that women’s tendency to partner with slightly older men shifted toward same-age partners as they grew older. Together, the findings do not establish a definitive rise in older women dating younger men, but they do suggest that the traditional older-man/younger-woman dating pattern may be less rigid than commonly assumed. Why these age-gap relationships can work Nelson said some women may feel more comfortable expressing their sexuality as they get older. "As women grow into their bodies, grow into their sexuality, we become less concerned with how other people see us," she said. "And then we discover that being sexy is an inside job." CLICK HERE FOR MORE HEALTH STORIES A 2026 Ashley Madison survey found that 45% of the dating site’s female members said they reached their sexual prime at age 40 or older. Nelson said her own conversations with age-gap couples suggest that men are drawn to older women because they may feel more comfortable communicating their sexual needs. Additionally, many women are entering a new phase of life after raising children, which means the younger men may face less pressure around marriage. "They're really participating as equal partners," Nelson said. "It comes back to this place where you realize you deserve pleasure," she added. "And what does pleasure look like? That's a whole new fun phase of life." Potential challenges That does not mean relationships between older women and younger men are without complications, particularly when couples are considering a long-term future. CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR HEALTH NEWSLETTER Differences in life stage, caregiving expectations and finances can create tension, according to Nelson. Couples may also have different views about marriage, children, retirement and long-term plans. Mismatched cultural references can pose another challenge. "It can be frustrating to be with someone who doesn't know who the Grateful Dead is, who's never been to a Rolling Stones concert or just doesn't know your level of cultural references," Nelson said. "There's something comforting about being with someone who grew up in the same world that you did." At the same time, those differences can create opportunities for couples to learn from each other, she noted. TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ "You can teach each other and share with each other a different perspective about the world," Nelson said. "And maybe share playlists with each other and discover new music." Ultimately, according to the expert, women should not assume that desire or intimacy has an expiration date. "If we're going to be alive, we want to feel alive."
